Twelve recipes for team marks in plotnine, the Python grammar of graphics: logo, wordmark and headshot layers, team color scales, facets, logo axes, title images, any image by URL, reference lines, tier lists and themes. Every sdvplot layer is an ordinary plotnine layer, so it composes with + like geom_point. The data is one season each from the WNBA and NBA (wehoop and hoopR), the NFL (nflverse), the NHL (fastRhockey) and men's college basketball, read from GitHub release files by sportsdataverse-py. import polars as pl import sportsdataverse.mbb as mbb import sportsdataverse.nba as nba import sportsdataverse.nfl as nfl import sportsdataverse.nhl as nhl import sportsdataverse.wnba as wnba from plotnine import ( aes, coord_flip, element_blank, element_line, element_rect, element_text, facet_wrap, geom_col, geom_hline, geom_line, geom_point, geom_text, ggplot, labs, scale_fill_manual, scale_x_continuous, scale_y_continuous, scale_y_reverse, theme, theme_bw, theme_minimal, ) import sdvplot from sdvplot.plotnine import ( geom_from_path, geom_mean_lines, geom_median_lines, geom_sdv_headshots, geom_sdv_logos, geom_sdv_wordmarks, scale_color_sdv, scale_fill_sdv, team_tiers, title_image, ) NFL_SEASON = 2025 # nflverse names a season by the year it starts SEASON = 2026 # the 2026 WNBA season and the 2025-26 NBA, NHL and college season NFLVERSE = "Data: nflverse via sportsdataverse-py" HOOPR = "Data: hoopR (ESPN) via sportsdataverse-py" WEHOOP = "Data: wehoop (ESPN) via sportsdataverse-py" FASTRHOCKEY = "Data: fastRhockey via sportsdataverse-py" The shared tables: WNBA team scoring per game (more than ten games drops the All-Star Game's teams), NFL EPA per play on offense and defense with each team's division, the NHL team box score, NBA team box scores and college basketball's adjusted efficiency with each team's conference. wnba_games = wnba.load_wnba_team_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).filter(pl.col("season_type") == 2) wnba_teams = ( wnba_games.group_by("team_abbreviation", maintain_order=True) .agg(games=pl.len(), scored=pl.col("team_score").mean(), allowed=pl.col("opponent_team_score").mean()) .filter(pl.col("games") > 10) .sort("team_abbreviation") ) nfl_weeks = nfl.load_nfl_team_stats([NFL_SEASON]).filter(pl.col("season_type") == "REG") plays = pl.col("attempts") + pl.col("sacks_suffered") + pl.col("carries") epa = pl.col("passing_epa") + pl.col("rushing_epa") nfl_epa = ( nfl_weeks.group_by("team", maintain_order=True) .agg(off_epa=epa.sum() / plays.sum()) .join( nfl_weeks.group_by(team=pl.col("opponent_team"), maintain_order=True).agg(def_epa=epa.sum() / plays.sum()), on="team", ) .join(nfl.load_nfl_teams().select(team="team_abbr", division="team_division"), on="team") .sort("team") ) nhl_games = nhl.load_nhl_team_box(seasons=[SEASON]).filter(pl.col("game_id") // 10_000 % 100 == 2) nba_box = nba.load_nba_team_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).filter(pl.col("season_type") == 2) mbb_ratings = ( mbb.load_mbb_ratings(SEASON) .join(sdvplot.teams("mbb").select("team_id", "conference"), on="team_id") .sort("team_id") ) wnba_teams.height, nfl_epa.height, nhl_games.height, nba_box.height, mbb_ratings.height (15, 32, 2624, 2470, 365)

Map the team column to the team aesthetic and add geom_sdv_logos(league=...). height is a fraction of the panel height. The layer trains the scales on the points, not on the images, so widen expand to keep the logos at the edges inside the panel. ( ggplot(wnba_teams, aes("scored", "allowed", team="team_abbreviation")) + geom_sdv_logos(league="wnba", height=0.1) + scale_x_continuous(expand=(0.06, 0)) + scale_y_reverse(expand=(0.08, 0)) + labs( x="Points scored per game", y="Points allowed per game (reversed: better is up)", title=f"WNBA scoring, {SEASON} regular season", caption=WEHOOP, ) + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(9, 6)) )

geom_sdv_wordmarks takes the same aesthetics; wordmarks are wide, so give them a smaller height. The archive has wordmarks for NFL and MLB teams; a team without one is skipped with a warning. Two NFC divisions: ( ggplot( nfl_epa.filter(pl.col("division").is_in(["NFC North", "NFC West"])), aes("off_epa", "def_epa", team="team"), ) + geom_sdv_wordmarks(league="nfl", height=0.06) + scale_y_reverse() + scale_x_continuous(expand=(0.15, 0)) + labs( x="Offense: EPA per play", y="Defense: EPA per play allowed", title=f"The NFC North and West, {NFL_SEASON}", caption=NFLVERSE, ) + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(9, 5)) )

geom_sdv_headshots maps player_id (ESPN athlete ids by default; NFL gsis ids with id_system="gsis"). geom_text, nudged to the right, names each one. The WNBA's top scorers: players = wnba.load_wnba_player_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( (pl.col("season_type") == 2) & ~pl.col("did_not_play") ) scorers = ( players.group_by("athlete_id", "athlete_display_name", maintain_order=True) .agg( games=pl.len(), ppg=pl.col("points").mean(), ts=pl.col("points").sum() / (2 * (pl.col("field_goals_attempted").sum() + 0.44 * pl.col("free_throws_attempted").sum())), ) .filter(pl.col("games") >= 25) .sort("ppg", descending=True) .head(10) .with_columns(name=pl.col("athlete_display_name").str.split(" ").list.last()) ) ( ggplot(scorers, aes("ppg", "ts", player_id="athlete_id")) + geom_sdv_headshots(league="wnba", height=0.1) + geom_text(aes(label="name"), nudge_x=0.3, ha="left", size=8) + scale_x_continuous(expand=(0.1, 0)) + scale_y_continuous(labels=lambda bs: [f"{b:.0%}" for b in bs], expand=(0.12, 0)) + labs( x="Points per game", y="True shooting %", title=f"WNBA top scorers, {SEASON} (25+ games)", caption=WEHOOP, ) + theme_bw() + theme(figure_size=(9, 6)) )

scale_fill_sdv(league) maps any team value to its primary color (which="secondary" for the other one); guide=None drops the legend the bars don't need. NHL power-play goals, top 12: power_play = ( nhl_games.group_by("team_abbrev", maintain_order=True) .agg(pl.col("power_play_goals").sum()) .sort(["power_play_goals", "team_abbrev"], descending=[True, False]) .head(12) ) ( ggplot(power_play, aes("reorder(team_abbrev, power_play_goals)", "power_play_goals", fill="team_abbrev")) + geom_col(width=0.7) + coord_flip() + scale_fill_sdv("nhl", guide=None) + labs(x="", y="Power-play goals", title="NHL power-play goals, 2025-26 (top 12)", caption=FASTRHOCKEY) + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(8, 5.5)) )

scale_color_sdv does the same for color, and keeps a legend when you want one. The AFC West's season as cumulative offensive EPA: afc_west = ( nfl_weeks.filter(pl.col("team").is_in(["DEN", "KC", "LAC", "LV"])) .sort("week") .with_columns(cum_epa=epa.cum_sum().over("team")) ) ( ggplot(afc_west, aes("week", "cum_epa", color="team")) + geom_hline(yintercept=0, color="grey") + geom_line(size=1.2) + geom_point(size=2) + scale_color_sdv("nfl", name="") + labs( x="Week", y="Cumulative offensive EPA", title=f"The AFC West's offenses, {NFL_SEASON}", caption=NFLVERSE, ) + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(9, 5.5)) )

The logo layer facets like any geom; each panel draws its own teams, and height is relative to the panel. Every NFL division: ( ggplot(nfl_epa, aes("off_epa", "def_epa", team="team")) + geom_hline(yintercept=0, color="#dddddd") + geom_sdv_logos(league="nfl", height=0.17) + facet_wrap("division", ncol=4) + scale_x_continuous(expand=(0.15, 0)) + scale_y_reverse(expand=(0.15, 0)) + labs( x="Offense: EPA per play", y="Defense: EPA per play allowed", title=f"NFL offense vs defense by division, {NFL_SEASON}", caption=NFLVERSE, ) + theme_bw() + theme(figure_size=(10, 6)) )

axis_logos (the front door, or sdvplot.plotnine.axis_logos) returns a copy of the plot whose team axis shows logos instead of labels. Map the team column to that axis; here ESPN team ids join the index's conference, cast from the raw integer so the join keys agree. east = sdvplot.teams("nba").filter(pl.col("conference") == "Eastern Conference").select("team_id") threes = ( nba_box.group_by("team_id", "team_abbreviation", maintain_order=True) .agg(games=pl.len(), fg3a=pl.col("three_point_field_goals_attempted").mean()) .filter(pl.col("games") > 10) .with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8)) .join(east, on="team_id") .sort("team_abbreviation") ) p = ( ggplot(threes, aes("reorder(team_abbreviation, -fg3a)", "fg3a", fill="team_abbreviation")) + geom_col(width=0.75) + scale_fill_sdv("nba", guide=None) + labs( x="", y="Three-point attempts per game", title="Eastern Conference three-point volume, 2025-26", caption=HOOPR ) # fmt: skip + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(10, 5)) ) sdvplot.axis_logos(p, "x", league="nba", height=0.09) For leagues with wordmarks in the archive (NFL, MLB), mark_type="wordmark" puts those on the axis instead.

Add title_image(team, title, league=...) after any labs; it replaces the title. One team's season, game by game: avs = ( nhl_games.filter(pl.col("team_abbrev") == "COL") .sort("game_date") .with_columns(game_no=pl.int_range(1, pl.len() + 1), margin=pl.col("goals") - pl.col("goals_against")) ) decided = avs.filter(pl.col("margin") != 0).with_columns( result=pl.when(pl.col("margin") > 0).then(pl.lit("Won")).otherwise(pl.lit("Lost")) ) shootouts = avs.height - decided.height colors = {"Won": sdvplot.team_colors("nhl", "COL"), "Lost": sdvplot.team_colors("nhl", "COL", which="secondary")} ( ggplot(decided, aes("game_no", "margin", fill="result")) + geom_col(width=0.8) + geom_hline(yintercept=0) + scale_fill_manual(values=colors, breaks=["Won", "Lost"]) + labs(x="Game", y="Goal margin", fill="", caption=f"{shootouts} games went to a shootout (no bar). {FASTRHOCKEY}") + title_image("COL", "Colorado's 2025-26, game by game", league="nhl", height=22) + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(10, 4.5), legend_position="top") ) result is not a team column, so scale_fill_sdv does not apply; a manual scale takes the team's two colors from team_colors instead. The box score's goals leave out the shootout, so those games (a margin of 0) are left out and counted in the caption.

geom_mean_lines(aes(x0=..., y0=...)) draws a vertical and a horizontal line at the means, per panel; geom_median_lines does the same at the medians. Both on one SEC chart: dashed grey at the mean, dotted red at the median. sec = mbb_ratings.filter(pl.col("conference") == "Southeastern Conference") ( ggplot(sec, aes("adj_o", "adj_d", team="team_id", x0="adj_o", y0="adj_d")) + geom_mean_lines(color="grey") + geom_median_lines(color="#c0392b", linetype="dotted") + geom_sdv_logos(league="mbb", height=0.09) + scale_y_reverse() + labs( x="Adjusted offense (points per 100)", y="Adjusted defense (points allowed per 100)", title="SEC adjusted efficiency, 2025-26", caption=HOOPR, ) + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(9, 6)) )

geom_from_path(aes(..., path=...)) draws any image by URL or local path, sized like the logo layers. Conferences are not teams, so their marks are ESPN's conference logo URLs. Every team's efficiency margin is a dot in its conference's row, and each row's logo sits at the left edge in place of a label. A polars Enum fixes the row order in all three layers. CONFERENCES = { "Southeastern Conference": "sec", "Big Ten Conference": "big_ten", "Big 12 Conference": "big_12", "Big East Conference": "big_east", "Atlantic Coast Conference": "acc", "Mountain West Conference": "mountain_west", "West Coast Conference": "west_coast", "Atlantic 10 Conference": "atlantic_10", "American Conference": "american", "Missouri Valley Conference": "missouri_valley", } members = mbb_ratings.filter(pl.col("conference").is_in(list(CONFERENCES))) means = members.group_by("conference", maintain_order=True).agg(pl.col("adj_em").mean()).sort("adj_em") rows = pl.Enum(means["conference"].to_list()) # weakest at the bottom, strongest on top members = members.with_columns(pl.col("conference").cast(rows)) means = means.with_columns( pl.col("conference").cast(rows), left=pl.lit(members["adj_em"].min() - 8), logo=pl.format( "https://a.espncdn.com/i/teamlogos/ncaa_conf/500/{}.png", pl.col("conference").cast(pl.String).replace_strict(CONFERENCES), ), ) ( ggplot(members, aes("adj_em", "conference")) + geom_point(color="#4a6fa5", alpha=0.45, size=2.5) + geom_point(data=means, shape="|", size=10, color="black") + geom_from_path(aes(x="left", path="logo"), data=means, height=0.075) + labs( x="Adjusted efficiency margin (each dot is a team; the bar is the conference average)", y="", title="Ten conferences, team by team, 2025-26", caption=f"{HOOPR}; conference logos: ESPN", ) + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(9, 6), axis_text_y=element_blank(), panel_grid_major_y=element_blank()) )
documents.s: 10. Any image, by URL: conference logos as row labels

documents.t: sdvplot.plotnine.team_tiers is the plotnine twin of the matplotlib tier list: same team / tier_no input, a ggplot out, so + theme(...) still works. NHL teams by goal differential per game: nhl_tiers = ( nhl_games.group_by("team_abbrev", maintain_order=True) .agg(gd=(pl.col("goals") - pl.col("goals_against")).mean()) .sort(["gd", "team_abbrev"], descending=[True, False]) .with_columns( team=pl.col("team_abbrev"), tier_no=pl.when(pl.col("gd") >= 0.5) .then(1) .when(pl.col("gd") >= 0.15) .then(2) .when(pl.col("gd") > -0.15) .then(3) .when(pl.col("gd") > -0.5) .then(4) .otherwise(5), ) ) ( team_tiers( nhl_tiers, "nhl", title="NHL tiers, 2025-26", subtitle="Goal differential per game", caption=FASTRHOCKEY, tier_desc={1: "+0.5 or more", 2: "+0.15 to +0.5", 3: "About even", 4: "-0.5 to -0.15", 5: "-0.5 or worse"}, ) + theme(figure_size=(9, 6)) )
documents.s: 11. A tier list as a ggplot

documents.t: Logos are drawn over whatever theme you use. On a dark background, variant="dark" picks marks made for dark grounds where the archive has them (others keep their default mark). The WNBA chart from recipe 1, dark: ink, ground, grid = "#e8e8e8", "#16191f", "#2b3038" ( ggplot(wnba_teams, aes("scored", "allowed", team="team_abbreviation", x0="scored", y0="allowed")) + geom_mean_lines(color="#6b7380") + geom_sdv_logos(league="wnba", variant="dark", height=0.1) + scale_x_continuous(expand=(0.06, 0)) + scale_y_reverse(expand=(0.08, 0)) + labs( x="Points scored per game", y="Points allowed per game", title=f"WNBA scoring, {SEASON}", caption=WEHOOP, ) + theme_minimal() + theme( figure_size=(9, 6), plot_background=element_rect(fill=ground, color=ground), panel_grid_major=element_line(color=grid), panel_grid_minor=element_blank(), text=element_text(color=ink), axis_text=element_text(color=ink), plot_title=element_text(weight="bold", size=14), ) )

plottable draws a table as a matplotlib figure: every cell is an axes, so a column can hold text, a bar or an image, and the finished table saves like any chart. sdvplot.plottable adds two ColumnDefinition builders: logo_column draws each row's team as its logo or wordmark (any variant, any season's mark) and headshot_column draws each row's player. sdvplot.team_colors supplies the colors for team-tinted rows. The Tables cookbook shows one MLB table with logos; these five recipes cover the WNBA, NFL, NHL, college football and men's college basketball, through sportsdataverse-py, and end with a square image sized for a social post. Saved images go to a temporary folder. import tempfile from pathlib import Path import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import polars as pl import sportsdataverse.cfb as cfb import sportsdataverse.mbb as mbb import sportsdataverse.nfl as nfl import sportsdataverse.nhl as nhl import sportsdataverse.wnba as wnba from IPython.display import Image, display from matplotlib import colormaps from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, to_rgba from plottable import ColumnDefinition, Table from plottable.cmap import normed_cmap from plottable.plots import bar import sdvplot from sdvplot.plottable import headshot_column, logo_column NFL_SEASON = 2025 # nflverse and cfbfastR name a season by the year it starts SEASON = 2026 # the 2026 WNBA season and the 2025-26 NHL and men's college basketball seasons OUT = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) # saved images go here, not into your working folder

headshot_column draws each row's player from an ESPN athlete id, and logo_column draws the team beside the name. The points column uses plottable's bar plot function, so each scoring average is a bar with its value written next to it. ESPN files the All-Star Game and the Commissioner's Cup final under the regular season too, so the box scores are first cut to the schedule's standard games, and the cell checks that no one played more games than a team's schedule holds. The 2026 regular season's top ten scorers with 20 or more games: # ESPN files the All-Star Game and the Commissioner's Cup final as regular-season games: keep the standard ones schedule = wnba.load_wnba_schedule(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( (pl.col("season_type") == 2) & (pl.col("type_abbreviation") == "STD") ) season_games = pl.concat([schedule["home_id"], schedule["away_id"]]).value_counts()["count"].max() players = wnba.load_wnba_player_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( pl.col("game_id").is_in(schedule["game_id"].implode()) & ~pl.col("did_not_play") ) per_player = ( players.sort("game_date") .group_by("athlete_id", "athlete_display_name", maintain_order=True) .agg( team=pl.col("team_abbreviation").last(), gp=pl.len(), ppg=pl.col("points").mean(), rpg=pl.col("rebounds").mean().round(1), apg=pl.col("assists").mean().round(1), ) ) assert per_player["gp"].max() <= season_games, "a player has more games than the schedule" scorers = ( per_player.filter(pl.col("gp") >= 20) .sort("ppg", descending=True) .head(10) .with_columns(rank=pl.int_range(1, 11)) .select( "rank", photo="athlete_id", player="athlete_display_name", logo="team", gp="gp", ppg="ppg", rpg="rpg", apg="apg" ) .to_pandas() .set_index("rank", drop=False) ) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 7)) Table( scorers, ax=ax, index_col="rank", column_definitions=[ ColumnDefinition("rank", title="", width=0.3), headshot_column("photo", league="wnba", title="", width=0.6), ColumnDefinition("player", title="Player", width=1.8, textprops={"ha": "left", "weight": "bold"}), logo_column("logo", league="wnba", title="", width=0.5), ColumnDefinition("gp", title="GP", width=0.4), ColumnDefinition( "ppg", title="Points per game", width=1.6, plot_fn=bar, plot_kw={ "xlim": (0, scorers["ppg"].max() * 1.1), "annotate": True, "color": "#e4572e", "height": 0.5, "formatter": "{:.1f}", }, ), ColumnDefinition("rpg", title="REB", width=0.5), ColumnDefinition("apg", title="AST", width=0.5), ], row_divider_kw={"linewidth": 0.5, "linestyle": (0, (1, 3))}, ) ax.set_title(f"The WNBA's top scorers, {SEASON}", loc="left", fontweight="bold", fontsize=14) fig.text(0.99, 0.01, "Data: wehoop (ESPN) via sportsdataverse-py", ha="right", fontsize=8, color="grey") plt.show()
documents.s: 1. Headshots and bars: the WNBA's leading scorers

documents.t: logo_column(mark_type="wordmark") draws the team's wordmark instead of its logo. The six EPA columns use plottable's cmap with normed_cmap, which centers each column's color scale on its mean: green is good, so the defensive columns take the reversed map. group= puts an Offense and a Defense header over their columns. The twelve best teams of 2025 by EPA per play: weeks = nfl.load_nfl_team_stats([NFL_SEASON]).filter(pl.col("season_type") == "REG") dropbacks = pl.col("attempts") + pl.col("sacks_suffered") def epa_rates(by): return weeks.group_by(team=by, maintain_order=True).agg( epa=(pl.col("passing_epa") + pl.col("rushing_epa")).sum() / (dropbacks + pl.col("carries")).sum(), pass_epa=pl.col("passing_epa").sum() / dropbacks.sum(), rush_epa=pl.col("rushing_epa").sum() / pl.col("carries").sum(), ) nfl_epa = ( epa_rates(pl.col("team")) .join(epa_rates(pl.col("opponent_team")), on="team", suffix="_allowed") .sort("epa", descending=True) .head(12) .to_pandas() .set_index("team", drop=False) ) good, bad = colormaps["PiYG"], colormaps["PiYG"].reversed() labels = {"epa": "Per play", "pass_epa": "Dropback", "rush_epa": "Carry"} fmt = "{:+.2f}" fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6.5)) Table( nfl_epa, ax=ax, index_col="team", column_definitions=[ logo_column("team", league="nfl", mark_type="wordmark", title="", width=1.4), *[ ColumnDefinition( c, title=labels[c], group="Offense: EPA", formatter=fmt, cmap=normed_cmap(nfl_epa[c], good) ) for c in labels ], *[ ColumnDefinition( f"{c}_allowed", title=labels[c], group="Defense: EPA allowed", formatter=fmt, cmap=normed_cmap(nfl_epa[f"{c}_allowed"], bad), ) for c in labels ], ], ) ax.set_title(f"The NFL's twelve best offenses by EPA per play, {NFL_SEASON}", loc="left", fontweight="bold") fig.text(0.99, 0.01, "Data: nflverse via sportsdataverse-py", ha="right", fontsize=8, color="grey") plt.show()
documents.s: 2. Wordmarks and color scales: NFL EPA

documents.t: sdvplot.team_colors returns each team's primary color, and after the table is drawn every row's cells take that color at a quarter opacity (table.rows[i].set_facecolor). The points-percentage column is a white bar over an outlined track (plot_bg_bar) on a 0 to 100% scale. The Atlantic Division's final 2025-26 standings: atlantic = ( nhl.nhl_standings("2026-04-16") .filter(pl.col("division_name") == "Atlantic") .sort("points", descending=True) .select( logo="team_abbrev_default", w="wins", l="losses", otl="ot_losses", pts="points", pct="point_pctg", gd="goal_differential", ) .to_pandas() .set_index("logo", drop=False) ) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6.5)) table = Table( atlantic, ax=ax, index_col="logo", column_definitions=[ logo_column("logo", league="nhl", title="", width=0.6), ColumnDefinition("w", title="W", width=0.5), ColumnDefinition("l", title="L", width=0.5), ColumnDefinition("otl", title="OTL", width=0.5), ColumnDefinition("pts", title="PTS", width=0.5, textprops={"weight": "bold"}), ColumnDefinition( "pct", title="Points %", width=1.4, plot_fn=bar, plot_kw={ "xlim": (0, 1), "plot_bg_bar": True, "annotate": True, "color": "#ffffff", "height": 0.4, "formatter": "{:.0%}", }, ), ColumnDefinition("gd", title="Goal diff.", width=0.7, formatter="{:+d}"), ], row_dividers=False, ) for i, color in enumerate(sdvplot.team_colors("nhl", atlantic["logo"].tolist())): table.rows[i].set_facecolor(to_rgba(color, 0.25)) ax.set_title(f"The Atlantic Division, {SEASON - 1}-{SEASON % 100}", loc="left", fontweight="bold") fig.text(0.99, 0.01, "Data: NHL standings via sportsdataverse-py", ha="right", fontsize=8, color="grey") plt.show()
documents.s: 3. Team-colored rows and track bars: an NHL division

documents.t: logo_column takes any id system sdvplot resolves; cfbfastR's ratings carry ESPN team ids, so the column reads them with id_system="espn" and no name lookup. Two rating systems sit under their own group headers, each column's text colored by its value (text_cmap with plottable's normed_cmap): green is good, red is poor, and the defensive columns use the reversed scale because allowing less is better. The top fifteen of 2025 by net adjusted EPA per play: summaries = cfb.load_cfb_team_summaries(NFL_SEASON).select("team_id", "pos_team", "conference") ratings = cfb.load_cfb_ratings(NFL_SEASON) assert summaries.schema["team_id"] == ratings.schema["team_id"] top15 = ( ratings.join(summaries, on="team_id") .sort("net_rank") .head(15) .select( "net_rank", logo="team_id", team="pos_team", conf="conference", off="adj_off_epa", dfn="adj_def_epa", net="adj_net", fei_off="fei_off", fei_def="fei_def", fei_net="fei_net", ) .to_pandas() .set_index("net_rank", drop=False) ) epa_fmt, fei_fmt = "{:+.3f}", "{:+.2f}" good = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("good", ["#b2182b", "#8c8c8c", "#1a7837"]) # dark enough to read as text def scale(column, cmap=good): """Color a column's text by its value, centered on its median.""" return normed_cmap(top15[column], cmap=cmap, num_stds=2) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8)) Table( top15, ax=ax, index_col="net_rank", column_definitions=[ ColumnDefinition("net_rank", title="#", width=0.3), logo_column("logo", league="cfb", id_system="espn", title="", width=0.5), ColumnDefinition("team", title="Team", width=1.4, textprops={"ha": "left", "weight": "bold"}), ColumnDefinition("conf", title="Conf.", width=1.5, textprops={"ha": "left", "color": "#555555"}), ColumnDefinition("off", title="Off.", group="Adjusted EPA per play", formatter=epa_fmt, text_cmap=scale("off")), ColumnDefinition( "dfn", title="Def.", group="Adjusted EPA per play", formatter=epa_fmt, text_cmap=scale("dfn", good.reversed()), ), ColumnDefinition( "net", title="Net", group="Adjusted EPA per play", formatter=epa_fmt, text_cmap=scale("net"), textprops={"weight": "bold"}, ), ColumnDefinition("fei_off", title="Off.", group="FEI", formatter=fei_fmt, text_cmap=scale("fei_off")), ColumnDefinition( "fei_def", title="Def.", group="FEI", formatter=fei_fmt, text_cmap=scale("fei_def", good.reversed()) ), ColumnDefinition( "fei_net", title="Net", group="FEI", formatter=fei_fmt, text_cmap=scale("fei_net"), textprops={"weight": "bold"}, ), ], even_row_color="#f6f6f6", ) ax.set_title(f"College football's best fifteen by adjusted EPA, {NFL_SEASON}", loc="left", fontweight="bold") fig.text(0.99, 0.01, "Data: cfbfastR via sportsdataverse-py", ha="right", fontsize=8, color="grey") plt.show()
documents.s: 4. Logos from ESPN ids: college football ratings

documents.t: A social post wants a fixed pixel size, and a plottable table is a matplotlib figure, so the size is the figure's inches times its dpi: 6 by 6 inches at 180 dpi is a 1080 by 1080 image. On a dark background logo_column's variant="dark" uses the logos drawn for one. The 2025-26 top ten in adjusted efficiency margin, saved to a file and shown from it: names = mbb.load_mbb_team_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).select("team_id", "team_location").unique("team_id") mbb_ratings = mbb.load_mbb_ratings(SEASON).with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Int32)) # ids ship as text here assert names.schema["team_id"] == mbb_ratings.schema["team_id"] top10 = ( mbb_ratings.sort("rank") .head(10) .join(names, on="team_id", how="left") .select("rank", logo="team_id", team="team_location", em="adj_em", o="adj_o", d="adj_d") .to_pandas() .set_index("rank", drop=False) ) BG, FG = "#14161a", "#e8e8e8" fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6), facecolor=BG) ax.set_facecolor(BG) Table( top10, ax=ax, index_col="rank", textprops={"color": FG, "fontsize": 11}, column_definitions=[ ColumnDefinition("rank", title="", width=0.3, textprops={"color": "#8a909a"}), logo_column("logo", league="mbb", id_system="espn", variant="dark", title="", width=0.5), ColumnDefinition("team", title="", width=1.5, textprops={"ha": "left", "weight": "bold"}), ColumnDefinition( "em", title="Margin", width=0.8, formatter="{:+.1f}", textprops={"color": "#7bd389", "weight": "bold"} ), ColumnDefinition("o", title="Off.", width=0.6, formatter="{:.1f}"), ColumnDefinition("d", title="Def.", width=0.6, formatter="{:.1f}"), ], col_label_divider_kw={"color": "#3a3f48"}, row_divider_kw={"color": "#2c3038", "linewidth": 0.6}, ) fig.suptitle( f"Men's college basketball, {SEASON - 1}-{SEASON % 100}", x=0.06, ha="left", color=FG, fontweight="bold", fontsize=15, ) fig.text(0.06, 0.915, "Top ten in adjusted efficiency margin (points per 100 possessions)", color="#a8adb7", fontsize=9) fig.text(0.94, 0.02, "Data: hoopR via sportsdataverse-py", ha="right", fontsize=8, color="#8a909a") path = OUT / "mbb_top10_square.png" fig.savefig(path, dpi=180, facecolor=BG) plt.close(fig) print(plt.imread(path).shape[1::-1]) display(Image(filename=path, width=540)) (1080, 1080)

pydeck draws deck.gl layers from Python: WebGL maps and charts that pan, zoom and tilt in the browser. sdvplot.pydeck builds three kinds of layer: team logos at points (logo_icon_layer), arcs in team colors (pass_arc_layer), and a sportypy rink, pitch, court or field in its own coordinates (surface_layer). Each returns pydeck.Layer's keyword arguments as a plain dict, and deck() puts them in a pydeck.Deck with its view fitted. The module needs pydeck: pip install "sdvplot[pydeck]". sdvplot-js builds the same layers for deck.gl in JavaScript, and the two are tested against one shared fixture. Every point here comes from a data source, never typed in: game 7 of the 2024 Stanley Cup Final from NHL api-web through sportsdataverse-py, the 2018 World Cup final from StatsBomb's open data, and MLB's ballparks from the MLB Stats API through sportsdataverse-py. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and hover a mark for its team. import polars as pl import pydeck as pdk import requests import sportsdataverse.mlb as mlb import sportsdataverse.nhl as nhl import sdvplot import sdvplot.pydeck as sdeck GAME = 2023030417 # game 7 of the 2024 Stanley Cup Final, Edmonton at Florida WORLD_CUP_FINAL = 8658 # StatsBomb's match id: France 4-2 Croatia, 2018-07-15 ESPN_TEAM = {"France": "478", "Croatia": "477"} # ESPN's soccer ids for the men's teams (2755 and 18889: the women's) MLB_SEASON = 2026 NHL api-web's play-by-play gives each shot in feet from centre ice, the frame sportypy draws its rink in, so the shots need no conversion. Its team ids are the NHL's own; the game's homeTeam and awayTeam name them. StatsBomb's events are in its 120 x 80 frame, which sdvplot.pitch_coords converts to sportypy's 105 x 68 m pitch (origin at the centre spot), flipping Croatia so the two teams attack opposite ends. StatsBomb open data is free for non-commercial use; credit it as below. raw = nhl.nhl_web_pbp(GAME, return_parsed=False) nhl_team = {t["id"]: t["abbrev"] for t in (raw["homeTeam"], raw["awayTeam"])} shots = ( nhl.parse_nhl_web_pbp(raw) .filter( pl.col("period_descriptor_number") == 1, pl.col("type_desc_key").is_in(["goal", "shot-on-goal", "missed-shot"]), ) .select( team=pl.col("details_event_owner_team_id").cast(pl.Int64).replace_strict(nhl_team), type=pl.col("type_desc_key"), time=pl.col("time_in_period"), x=pl.col("details_x_coord"), y=pl.col("details_y_coord"), ) # the goal each shot was aimed at: the goal line is 89 ft from centre, at the end the shot came from .with_columns(net_x=pl.col("x").sign() * 89, net_y=pl.lit(0.0)) ) events = requests.get( f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/statsbomb/open-data/master/data/events/{WORLD_CUP_FINAL}.json", timeout=60 ).json() completed = [e for e in events if e["type"]["name"] == "Pass" and "outcome" not in e["pass"]] passes = pl.DataFrame( { "team": [ESPN_TEAM[e["team"]["name"]] for e in completed], "half": [e["period"] for e in completed], "x": [e["location"][0] for e in completed], "y": [e["location"][1] for e in completed], "end_x": [e["pass"]["end_location"][0] for e in completed], "end_y": [e["pass"]["end_location"][1] for e in completed], } ).with_columns(croatia=pl.col("team") == ESPN_TEAM["Croatia"]) start = sdvplot.pitch_coords(passes, provider="statsbomb", flip="croatia") end = sdvplot.pitch_coords(passes, provider="statsbomb", x="end_x", y="end_y", flip="croatia") passes = start.with_columns(to_x=end["pitch_x"], to_y=end["pitch_y"]) teams = mlb.mlb_teams(season=MLB_SEASON, hydrate="venue(location)")["teams"] parks = pl.DataFrame( [ { "team": t["abbreviation"], "park": t["venue"]["name"], "longitude": t["venue"]["location"]["defaultCoordinates"]["longitude"], "latitude": t["venue"]["location"]["defaultCoordinates"]["latitude"], } for t in teams ] ).sort("team") shots.height, passes.height, parks.height (27, 650, 30)

surface_layer("hockey", "nhl") is sportypy's NHL rink as a PolygonLayer in feet, the origin at centre ice, and logo_icon_layer puts each shot's team logo at its (x, y) in the same feet. deck() sees the surface, draws it top down (an OrthographicView, y up) fitted to the rink, and draws the logos in the rink's coordinates. size is the logo's height on screen in pixels. In the first period Edmonton shot at the right-hand goal and Florida at the left. pydeck writes every layer's data into the page, so tolerance (in feet here) thins sportypy's arcs further than the default: at 0.25 ft the rink is about 9,200 points instead of 14,400 (123,000 unthinned). Each line keeps its shape, because each loop caps the tolerance at its own width and keeps its corners. rink = sdeck.surface_layer("hockey", "nhl", tolerance=0.25) logos = sdeck.logo_icon_layer(shots, x="x", y="y", team="team", league="nhl", size=26) sdeck.deck(rink, logos, height=420, tooltip={"text": "{team}"})
documents.s: 1. Every shot of a Stanley Cup Final period, as logos on the rink

documents.t: pass_arc_layer draws one arc per row from (x, y) to (xend, yend), in the team's colors: its primary color where the arc starts and its secondary where it ends, so each arc shows its direction (no background here, so the colors are the teams' own). deck.gl's arcs stand upright by default, which a top-down view sees as straight lines; tilt=90 lays them flat on the ice, and height=0.3 keeps each curve low (deck.gl's default height, 1, swings a long arc well past the boards). arcs = sdeck.pass_arc_layer( shots, x="x", y="y", xend="net_x", yend="net_y", team="team", league="nhl", width=3, tilt=90, height=0.3 ) sdeck.deck(rink, arcs, height=420)
documents.s: 2. Each shot as an arc to the goal it was aimed at

documents.t: The pitch is surface_layer("soccer", "fifa") resized to the 105 x 68 m frame pitch_coords returns, through sportypy's own pitch_updates. France's completed first-half passes, each from where it was played to where it was received, attacking left to right. Without background the colors are the team's own: France's navy and its secondary color. pitch = sdeck.surface_layer("soccer", "fifa", pitch_updates={"pitch_length": 105, "pitch_width": 68}) france = passes.filter(pl.col("team") == ESPN_TEAM["France"], pl.col("half") == 1) arcs = sdeck.pass_arc_layer( france, x="pitch_x", y="pitch_y", xend="to_x", yend="to_y", team="team", league="soccer", id_system="team_id", tilt=90, height=0.3, width=2, ) # fmt: skip print(f"{france.height} passes") sdeck.deck(pitch, arcs, height=440) 89 passes
documents.s: 3. France's passes in the 2018 World Cup final, flat on the pitch

documents.t: The arcs are drawn on the pitch's green, so pass it as background: every color then keeps 3:1 contrast against the grass (WCAG's minimum for graphics), a team color that would not read gives way to the team's other color or is lightened until it does, and the two teams' colors stay distinct (a CIE76 ΔE of 20 or more). This is the same team palette sdvplot-js uses for dark mode. Croatia's passes are flipped to attack right to left. One caveat: a color that does not read gives way to the team's other color, so when only one of a team's two colors reads on the background, both ends take it. France's navy does not read on this dark grass, so its passes are mint at both ends (the printed colors show it) and their direction is lost, while Croatia's two colors both read (lightened) and its arcs keep theirs. On a grass where both of a team's colors read, the ends differ: check sourceColor against targetColor. grass = "#{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}".format(*pitch["data"][0]["fillColor"][:3]) # the pitch's own fill first_half = passes.filter(pl.col("half") == 1) arcs = sdeck.pass_arc_layer( first_half, x="pitch_x", y="pitch_y", xend="to_x", yend="to_y", team="team", league="soccer", id_system="team_id", tilt=90, height=0.3, background=grass, ) # fmt: skip print(grass, {d["team"]: (d["sourceColor"], d["targetColor"]) for d in arcs["data"]}) sdeck.deck(pitch, arcs, height=440) #195f0c {'477': ([255, 127, 127, 255], [146, 161, 255, 255]), '478': ([200, 230, 216, 255], [200, 230, 216, 255])}
documents.s: 4. Both finalists, readable on the grass

documents.t: Without tilt, deck.gl's arcs rise off the surface, higher for longer passes, and a tilted view shows them. deck() draws top down, so build the pydeck.Deck yourself with an OrbitView. The layers are pydeck.Layer keyword arguments: a constant string is quoted ("'cartesian'"), because pydeck reads an unquoted string as an expression. France's second-half passes: second = passes.filter(pl.col("team") == ESPN_TEAM["France"], pl.col("half") == 2) arcs = sdeck.pass_arc_layer( second, x="pitch_x", y="pitch_y", xend="to_x", yend="to_y", team="team", league="soccer", id_system="team_id", background=grass, ) # fmt: skip pdk.Deck( layers=[pdk.Layer(**pitch), pdk.Layer(**arcs, coordinate_system="'cartesian'")], views=[pdk.View(type="OrbitView", controller=True)], initial_view_state=pdk.ViewState(target=[0, 0, 0], rotation_x=40, rotation_orbit=-20, zoom=2.4), map_provider=None, height=440, )

Without a surface, deck() draws a map fitted to the layers' positions, so x is a longitude and y a latitude. Every MLB ballpark, from the MLB Stats API's venue coordinates; its abbreviations (AZ, CWS) resolve to the same teams as ESPN's. logos = sdeck.logo_icon_layer(parks, x="longitude", y="latitude", team="team", league="mlb", size=34) sdeck.deck(logos, height=440, map_style="light", tooltip={"text": "{team}"})

surface_layer draws all ten of sportypy's sports, lacrosse, softball and volleyball included. The NLL plays box lacrosse on a rink with boards, in feet with the origin at its centre, as the hockey rink above. With no other layer, deck() fits the view to the surface. box = sdeck.surface_layer("lacrosse", "nll") sdeck.deck(box, height=360) Data: NHL api-web; StatsBomb open data; the MLB Stats API.

pygal draws charts as SVG, with hover tooltips built in. sdvplot adds two things to it: sdvplot.pygal.team_style() turns a list of teams into a pygal Style whose series colors are the team colors, and add_logos / add_wordmarks / add_headshots place images on any XY-family chart (XY, DateLine, DateTimeLine, ...) at the exact spot pygal draws each point. pygal writes axis labels as text, so there are no axis logos; axis_logos raises a TypeError that says so. The data is one completed season each from the NFL (nflverse), MLB (ESPN), the NBA and men's college basketball (hoopR), the WNBA (wehoop) and the NHL (fastRhockey), all through sportsdataverse-py. import polars as pl import pygal import sportsdataverse.mbb as mbb import sportsdataverse.mlb as mlb import sportsdataverse.nba as nba import sportsdataverse.nfl as nfl import sportsdataverse.nhl as nhl import sportsdataverse.wnba as wnba from IPython.display import HTML, Image, display import sdvplot import sdvplot.pygal NFL_SEASON = 2025 # football names a season by the year it starts SEASON = 2026 # the 2026 MLB and WNBA seasons, and the 2025-26 NBA, NHL and college basketball season def show_svg(chart): """Show a pygal chart inline as SVG (the logos are drawn while pygal renders).""" display(HTML(chart.render(is_unicode=True, disable_xml_declaration=True))) def pad(values, share=0.08): """An axis range with room at both ends, so the logos at the edges are not cut off.""" lo, hi = min(values), max(values) return lo - (hi - lo) * share, hi + (hi - lo) * share pygal's own notebook display is a PNG through cairosvg; show_svg keeps the chart as SVG so its tooltips work. Every chart below renders with the logos, because sdvplot hooks into pygal's render step rather than editing one finished SVG.

A pygal scatter is an XY chart with stroke=False. Give each point a label so pygal's tooltip names the team, then call add_logos with the same x and y. NFL offense against defense, EPA per play: weeks = nfl.load_nfl_team_stats([NFL_SEASON]).filter(pl.col("season_type") == "REG") plays = pl.col("attempts") + pl.col("sacks_suffered") + pl.col("carries") epa = pl.col("passing_epa") + pl.col("rushing_epa") nfl_epa = ( weeks.group_by("team", maintain_order=True) .agg(off_epa=epa.sum() / plays.sum()) .join( weeks.group_by(team=pl.col("opponent_team"), maintain_order=True).agg(def_epa=epa.sum() / plays.sum()), on="team", ) .sort("team") ) chart = pygal.XY( stroke=False, width=800, height=560, dots_size=3, show_legend=False, xrange=pad(nfl_epa["off_epa"]), range=pad(nfl_epa["def_epa"]), title=f"NFL EPA per play, {NFL_SEASON} regular season (lower defense EPA is better)", x_title="Offense EPA per play", y_title="Defense EPA per play allowed", ) # fmt: skip chart.add("teams", [{"value": (o, d), "label": t} for t, o, d in nfl_epa.iter_rows()]) sdvplot.add_logos(chart, nfl_epa["off_epa"], nfl_epa["def_epa"], nfl_epa["team"], league="nfl", height=0.08) show_svg(chart)

add_wordmarks takes the same arguments as add_logos. A wordmark is wider than it is tall, so a smaller height keeps neighbours apart, and a wordmark with a lot of empty space around its letters draws small. MLB runs scored and allowed per game: mlb_runs = ( mlb.espn_mlb_standings(season=SEASON) .with_columns( rs=pl.col("points_for") / pl.col("games_played"), ra=pl.col("points_against") / pl.col("games_played") ) .sort("team_abbreviation") ) chart = pygal.XY( stroke=False, width=800, height=560, dots_size=2, show_legend=False, xrange=pad(mlb_runs["rs"]), range=pad(mlb_runs["ra"]), title=f"MLB runs scored and allowed per game, {SEASON}", x_title="Runs scored per game", y_title="Runs allowed per game", ) # fmt: skip chart.add( "teams", [{"value": (s, a), "label": t} for t, s, a in mlb_runs.select("team_abbreviation", "rs", "ra").iter_rows()] ) sdvplot.add_wordmarks(chart, mlb_runs["rs"], mlb_runs["ra"], mlb_runs["team_abbreviation"], league="mlb", height=0.07) show_svg(chart)

team_style() works on every pygal chart, not only XY: it returns a Style whose colors follow the order you add the series. Add one series per team and each bar takes its team's primary color; a label on each value and print_labels=True write the team on its bar. The ten NBA teams that took the most threes per game: nba_threes = ( nba.load_nba_team_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]) .filter(pl.col("season_type") == 2) .group_by("team_id", "team_abbreviation", maintain_order=True) .agg(games=pl.len(), fg3a=pl.col("three_point_field_goals_attempted").mean()) .filter(pl.col("games") > 10) .with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8)) .sort("fg3a", descending=True) .head(10) ) style = sdvplot.pygal.team_style(nba_threes["team_id"], league="nba", font_family="sans-serif") chart = pygal.Bar( style=style, width=800, height=480, show_legend=False, print_labels=True, title=f"NBA three-point attempts per game, {SEASON - 1}-{SEASON % 100} (top 10)", y_title="3PA per game", ) # fmt: skip for team, fg3a in nba_threes.select("team_abbreviation", "fg3a").iter_rows(): chart.add(team, [{"value": round(fg3a, 1), "label": team}]) show_svg(chart)
documents.s: 3. Team colors on a bar chart

documents.t: add_headshots places ESPN headshots by athlete id. WNBA scoring leaders, points per game against minutes per game (players with at least 20 games): # ESPN files the All-Star Game and the Commissioner's Cup final as regular-season games: keep the standard ones schedule = wnba.load_wnba_schedule(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( (pl.col("season_type") == 2) & (pl.col("type_abbreviation") == "STD") ) season_games = pl.concat([schedule["home_id"], schedule["away_id"]]).value_counts()["count"].max() per_player = ( wnba.load_wnba_player_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]) .filter( pl.col("game_id").is_in(schedule["game_id"].implode()) & pl.col("did_not_play").not_() & pl.col("minutes").is_not_null() ) .group_by("athlete_id", "athlete_display_name", maintain_order=True) .agg(games=pl.len(), mpg=pl.col("minutes").mean(), ppg=pl.col("points").mean()) ) assert per_player["games"].max() <= season_games, "a player has more games than the schedule" wnba_players = ( per_player.filter(pl.col("games") >= 20) .sort("ppg", descending=True) .head(12) .with_columns(pl.col("athlete_id").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8)) ) chart = pygal.XY( stroke=False, width=800, height=560, dots_size=2, show_legend=False, xrange=pad(wnba_players["mpg"]), range=pad(wnba_players["ppg"], 0.12), title=f"WNBA scoring leaders, {SEASON}", x_title="Minutes per game", y_title="Points per game", ) # fmt: skip chart.add( "players", [ {"value": (m, p), "label": n} for n, m, p in wnba_players.select("athlete_display_name", "mpg", "ppg").iter_rows() ], ) sdvplot.add_headshots( chart, wnba_players["mpg"], wnba_players["ppg"], wnba_players["athlete_id"], league="wnba", height=0.1 ) show_svg(chart)

DateLine is in the XY family, so the logos take dates for x. Here team_style() colors the lines and add_logos marks where each team finished. Cumulative wins in the standard games of the schedule above, for four WNBA teams spread evenly from the top of the standings to the bottom: wnba_games = ( wnba.load_wnba_team_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]) .filter(pl.col("game_id").is_in(schedule["game_id"].implode())) .sort("game_date") .with_columns(wins=pl.col("team_winner").cast(pl.Int64).cum_sum().over("team_abbreviation")) ) standings = ( wnba_games.group_by("team_abbreviation") .agg(pl.col("wins").max()) .sort(["wins", "team_abbreviation"], descending=[True, False]) )["team_abbreviation"] n = standings.len() leaders = standings.gather([round(i * (n - 1) / 3) for i in range(4)]).to_list() # first, last and two between ends_max = wnba_games["wins"].max() chart = pygal.DateLine( style=sdvplot.pygal.team_style(leaders, league="wnba"), width=800, height=480, dots_size=2, x_label_rotation=25, legend_at_bottom=True, range=(0, ends_max * 1.12), y_title="Wins", title=f"WNBA cumulative wins, {SEASON}", ) # fmt: skip ends = [] for team in leaders: rows = wnba_games.filter(pl.col("team_abbreviation") == team).select("game_date", "wins") chart.add(team, list(rows.iter_rows())) ends.append(rows.row(-1)) sdvplot.add_logos(chart, [d for d, _ in ends], [w for _, w in ends], leaders, league="wnba", height=0.09) show_svg(chart)
documents.s: 5. A date line: team colors and a logo at the end of each line

documents.t: team_style() passes any other Style option through, so one call sets the team colors and a dark background. variant="dark" picks each team's logo drawn for dark backgrounds. NHL goals for and against per game, with each team its own series so its dot takes its secondary color (the logos name the teams, so the legend is off): nhl_teams = ( nhl.load_nhl_team_box(seasons=[SEASON]) .filter(pl.col("game_id") // 10_000 % 100 == 2) .group_by("team_abbrev", maintain_order=True) .agg(gf=pl.col("goals").mean(), ga=pl.col("goals_against").mean()) .sort("team_abbrev") ) dark = sdvplot.pygal.team_style( nhl_teams["team_abbrev"], league="nhl", which="secondary", background="#15171c", plot_background="#15171c", foreground="#d6d8de", foreground_strong="#ffffff", foreground_subtle="#3a3e48", ) # fmt: skip chart = pygal.XY( style=dark, stroke=False, width=800, height=560, dots_size=4, show_legend=False, xrange=pad(nhl_teams["gf"]), range=pad(nhl_teams["ga"]), title=f"NHL goals for and against per game, {SEASON - 1}-{SEASON % 100}", x_title="Goals for per game", y_title="Goals against per game", inverse_y_axis=True, ) # fmt: skip for team, gf, ga in nhl_teams.iter_rows(): chart.add(team, [(gf, ga)]) sdvplot.add_logos( chart, nhl_teams["gf"], nhl_teams["ga"], nhl_teams["team_abbrev"], league="nhl", variant="dark", height=0.07 ) show_svg(chart)
documents.s: 6. A dark chart with dark-background logos

documents.t: pygal's render_to_png() rasterizes the SVG with cairosvg. cairosvg does not fetch linked images, so pass embed=True: sdvplot puts each logo in the SVG as a data URI and the PNG needs no network. The SEC's adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency: sec = ( mbb.load_mbb_ratings(SEASON) .join( sdvplot.teams("mbb").filter(pl.col("conference") == "Southeastern Conference").select("team_id", "name"), on="team_id", ) .sort("team_id") ) chart = pygal.XY( stroke=False, width=900, height=640, dots_size=2, show_legend=False, xrange=pad(sec["adj_o"]), range=pad(sec["adj_d"]), title=f"SEC adjusted efficiency, {SEASON - 1}-{SEASON % 100}", x_title="Adjusted offense (points per 100)", y_title="Adjusted defense (points allowed per 100)", inverse_y_axis=True, ) # fmt: skip chart.add("teams", [{"value": (o, d), "label": n} for n, o, d in sec.select("name", "adj_o", "adj_d").iter_rows()]) sdvplot.add_logos( chart, sec["adj_o"], sec["adj_d"], sec["team_id"], league="mbb", season=SEASON, height=0.08, embed=True ) display(Image(data=chart.render_to_png(dpi=144), width=760))

reactable-py is the Python port of R's reactable: an interactive HTML table with sorting, searching, paging, grouped rows with aggregates, expandable row details, column groups and themes. sdvplot.reactable adds the SportsDataverse marks to it as ordinary reactable.Column objects: team logos and wordmarks, player headshots, logos in column headers, and cells tinted or barred in each row's team color. These six recipes build on the Tables cookbook's single example (logos and team-color bars on NBA wins) with the parts it does not show, across the WNBA, NFL, NHL, college football and men's college basketball, all loaded through sportsdataverse-py. import warnings import polars as pl import sportsdataverse.cfb as cfb import sportsdataverse.mbb as mbb import sportsdataverse.nfl as nfl import sportsdataverse.nhl as nhl import sportsdataverse.wnba as wnba from matplotlib import colormaps from reactable import ColGroup, Column, Reactable, Theme, embed_css import sdvplot from sdvplot.reactable import ( reactable_sdv_cols_label, reactable_sdv_headshots, reactable_sdv_logos, reactable_sdv_team_color_bg, reactable_sdv_wordmarks, ) NFL_SEASON = 2025 # nflverse and cfbfastR name a season by the year it starts SEASON = 2026 # the 2026 WNBA season and the 2025-26 NHL and men's college basketball seasons embed_css() def heat(frame, column, cmap="RdYlGn", reverse=False, alpha=0.55): """A reactable ``style`` function: each cell's background on a color scale over the column's range.""" lo, hi = frame[column].min(), frame[column].max() scale = colormaps[cmap].reversed() if reverse else colormaps[cmap] def style(info): r, g, b, _ = scale((info.value - lo) / (hi - lo)) return {"background-color": f"rgba({r * 255:.0f}, {g * 255:.0f}, {b * 255:.0f}, {alpha})"} return style

reactable_sdv_headshots turns a column of ESPN athlete ids into player photos, and reactable_sdv_team_color_bg fills another column with each row's team color at low opacity, so the player's name sits on a tint of the team they finished the season with. Both read the team from a column of the same frame: here team, which the table hides once it has done that job. ESPN files the All-Star Game and the Commissioner's Cup final under the regular season too, so the box scores are first cut to the schedule's standard games, and the cell checks that no one played more games than a team's schedule holds. The 2026 regular season, 20 or more games: # ESPN files the All-Star Game and the Commissioner's Cup final as regular-season games: keep the standard ones schedule = wnba.load_wnba_schedule(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( (pl.col("season_type") == 2) & (pl.col("type_abbreviation") == "STD") ) season_games = pl.concat([schedule["home_id"], schedule["away_id"]]).value_counts()["count"].max() players = wnba.load_wnba_player_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( pl.col("game_id").is_in(schedule["game_id"].implode()) & ~pl.col("did_not_play") ) per_player = ( players.sort("game_date") .group_by("athlete_id", "athlete_display_name", maintain_order=True) .agg( team=pl.col("team_abbreviation").last(), gp=pl.len(), ppg=pl.col("points").mean().round(1), rpg=pl.col("rebounds").mean().round(1), apg=pl.col("assists").mean().round(1), ) ) assert per_player["gp"].max() <= season_games, "a player has more games than the schedule" leaders = ( per_player.filter(pl.col("gp") >= 20) .sort("ppg", descending=True) .head(15) .with_columns(photo=pl.col("athlete_id"), logo=pl.col("team")) .select("photo", "athlete_display_name", "logo", "team", "gp", "ppg", "rpg", "apg") ) Reactable( leaders, columns=[ reactable_sdv_headshots(league="wnba", id="photo", name="", width=70, height=44), reactable_sdv_team_color_bg( leaders, "team", league="wnba", alpha=0.3, id="athlete_display_name", name="Player", min_width=190 ), reactable_sdv_logos(league="wnba", id="logo", name="", width=50, height=26), Column(id="team", show=False), Column(id="gp", name="GP"), Column(id="ppg", name="PTS"), Column(id="rpg", name="REB"), Column(id="apg", name="AST"), ], default_page_size=15, default_col_def=Column(v_align="center"), highlight=True, compact=True, )

reactable_sdv_wordmarks shows each team as its wordmark instead of its logo; NFL teams have one for every club. Here it heads an offense-versus-defense table built from nflverse's weekly team stats: expected points added per dropback and per carry, for each team's offense and for what its defense allowed. ColGroup puts a spanning header over each side, and a small heat style function (defined above) colors every cell on the column's range: green is good, so the defensive columns use the reversed scale. Click any header to re-sort. weeks = nfl.load_nfl_team_stats([NFL_SEASON]).filter(pl.col("season_type") == "REG") dropbacks = pl.col("attempts") + pl.col("sacks_suffered") def epa_rates(by): return weeks.group_by(team=by, maintain_order=True).agg( epa=(pl.col("passing_epa") + pl.col("rushing_epa")).sum() / (dropbacks + pl.col("carries")).sum(), pass_epa=pl.col("passing_epa").sum() / dropbacks.sum(), rush_epa=pl.col("rushing_epa").sum() / pl.col("carries").sum(), ) nfl_epa = ( epa_rates(pl.col("team")) .join(epa_rates(pl.col("opponent_team")), on="team", suffix="_allowed") .with_columns(pl.selectors.float().round(3), mark=pl.col("team")) .sort("epa", descending=True) .select("mark", "team", "epa", "pass_epa", "rush_epa", "epa_allowed", "pass_epa_allowed", "rush_epa_allowed") ) offense = ["epa", "pass_epa", "rush_epa"] defense = [f"{c}_allowed" for c in offense] labels = {"epa": "Per play", "pass_epa": "Per dropback", "rush_epa": "Per carry"} Reactable( nfl_epa, columns=[ reactable_sdv_wordmarks(league="nfl", id="mark", name="", height=22, width=150), Column(id="team", show=False), *[Column(id=c, name=labels[c], style=heat(nfl_epa, c), align="center") for c in offense], *[ Column(id=c, name=labels[c.removesuffix("_allowed")], style=heat(nfl_epa, c, reverse=True), align="center") for c in defense ], ], column_groups=[ ColGroup(name="Offense: EPA", columns=offense), ColGroup(name="Defense: EPA allowed", columns=defense), ], default_page_size=12, compact=True, )
documents.s: 2. Wordmarks, column groups and heat cells: NFL EPA

documents.t: reactable groups rows with group_by and fills each group's header row with the column's aggregate. With reactable_sdv_logos(include_name=True) the team column keeps its abbreviation after the logo, so the four division groups of the NHL's final 2025-26 standings read as one table: each group row sums its teams' wins, losses, points and goal differential. Collapse a division by clicking its row. nhl_table = ( nhl.nhl_standings("2026-04-16") .select( division="division_name", team="team_abbrev_default", gp="games_played", w="wins", l="losses", otl="ot_losses", pts="points", gd="goal_differential", ) .sort(["division", "pts", "team"], descending=[False, True, False]) ) Reactable( nhl_table, group_by="division", columns=[ Column(id="division", name="Division", min_width=150), reactable_sdv_logos(league="nhl", id="team", name="Team", include_name=True, height=24, min_width=110), Column(id="gp", name="GP", aggregate="sum"), Column(id="w", name="W", aggregate="sum"), Column(id="l", name="L", aggregate="sum"), Column(id="otl", name="OTL", aggregate="sum"), Column(id="pts", name="PTS", aggregate="sum"), Column(id="gd", name="Goal diff.", aggregate="sum"), ], default_expanded=True, pagination=False, compact=True, )
documents.s: 3. Grouped rows with aggregates: NHL standings by division

documents.t: reactable_sdv_cols_label makes one column per team-named column of a frame, its header the team's logo. That fits a matrix: one row and one column per team, each cell the row team's combined point margin over its two games against the column team in the 2025 regular season. Pass it only the team-named columns; the extra keyword arguments (a margin color and an empty-cell text) go to every column it makes. division = ["CHI", "DET", "GB", "MIN"] games = nfl.load_nfl_schedule([NFL_SEASON]).filter( (pl.col("game_type") == "REG") & pl.col("home_team").is_in(division) & pl.col("away_team").is_in(division) ) sides = [("home_team", "away_team", "home_score", "away_score"), ("away_team", "home_team", "away_score", "home_score")] margins = pl.concat(games.select(team=pl.col(t), opp=pl.col(o), margin=pl.col(a) - pl.col(b)) for t, o, a, b in sides) matrix = ( margins.group_by("team", "opp") .agg(pl.col("margin").sum()) .pivot(on="opp", index="team", values="margin") .select("team", *division) .sort("team") ) def margin_color(info): if info.value is None: return {"background-color": "#f2f2f2"} return {"color": "#1a7f37" if info.value > 0 else "#c0392b", "font-weight": "600"} Reactable( matrix, columns=[ reactable_sdv_logos(league="nfl", id="team", name="", height=34, width=80), *reactable_sdv_cols_label( matrix.select(division), league="nfl", height=34, style=margin_color, align="center", v_align="center", na="", width=90, ), ], bordered=True, sortable=False, )
documents.s: 4. Logos in the column headers: an NFC North head-to-head

documents.t: A details column renders extra content under a row when you expand it. Each row here is an SEC team in cfbfastR's 2025 adjusted ratings (net adjusted EPA per play, with its national rank), logo first; expanding it lists the team's completed games, each opponent drawn by its logo from sdvplot.logo_url. The detail function runs once per row when the table is built, so the page needs no Python to open a row. ratings = cfb.load_cfb_ratings(NFL_SEASON).select("team_id", "net_rank", "adj_off_epa", "adj_def_epa", "adj_net") sec_teams = cfb.load_cfb_team_summaries(NFL_SEASON).filter(pl.col("conference") == "SEC").select("team_id", "pos_team") assert sec_teams.schema["team_id"] == ratings.schema["team_id"] sec = ( sec_teams.join(ratings, on="team_id") .with_columns(pl.selectors.float().round(3), logo=pl.col("team_id")) .sort("adj_net", descending=True) .select("logo", "pos_team", "net_rank", "adj_off_epa", "adj_def_epa", "adj_net", "team_id") ) schedule = cfb.load_cfb_schedule(NFL_SEASON).filter(pl.col("completed")) results = pl.concat( schedule.select( "week", team_id=pl.col(f"{us}_id"), opp_id=pl.col(f"{them}_id"), opp=pl.col(f"{them}_team"), pts=pl.col(f"{us}_points"), opp_pts=pl.col(f"{them}_points"), ) for us, them in [("home", "away"), ("away", "home")] ).sort("team_id", "week") by_team = results.partition_by("team_id", as_dict=True) def game_html(game): with warnings.catch_warnings(): # an opponent without a logo keeps its name instead warnings.simplefilter("ignore", sdvplot.SdvplotWarning) url = sdvplot.logo_url(game["opp_id"], "cfb", id_system="espn") mark = f'' if url else game["opp"] won = game["pts"] > game["opp_pts"] return ( f'{mark}' f'{"W" if won else "L"}' f" {game['pts']}-{game['opp_pts']}" ) def details(row): team_id = sec["team_id"][row.row_index] return "".join(game_html(g) for g in by_team[(team_id,)].iter_rows(named=True)) Reactable( sec, columns=[ reactable_sdv_logos(league="cfb", id="logo", name="", id_system="espn", height=28, width=60), Column(id="pos_team", name="Team", min_width=140), Column(id="net_rank", name="Natl. rank"), Column(id="adj_off_epa", name="Off. EPA/play"), Column(id="adj_def_epa", name="Def. EPA/play"), Column(id="adj_net", name="Net"), Column(id="team_id", show=False), ], details=Column(details=details, html=True), default_page_size=16, highlight=True, compact=True, )
documents.s: 5. Expandable row details: the SEC's games

documents.t: reactable's Theme restyles the whole table, and reactable_sdv_logos(variant="dark") swaps in the logo variant drawn for dark backgrounds, so the marks stay readable on it. The table is the top 25 of the 2025-26 adjusted efficiency ratings from hoopR's men's college basketball data: adjusted offense and defense (points per 100 possessions) carry heat cells, with the defensive scale reversed because fewer points allowed is better. names = mbb.load_mbb_team_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).select("team_id", "team_location").unique("team_id") mbb_ratings = mbb.load_mbb_ratings(SEASON).with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Int32)) # ids ship as text here assert names.schema["team_id"] == mbb_ratings.schema["team_id"] top25 = ( mbb_ratings.sort("rank") .head(25) .join(names, on="team_id", how="left") .with_columns(pl.col("adj_em", "adj_o", "adj_d", "adj_tempo").round(1), logo=pl.col("team_id")) .select("rank", "logo", "team_location", "adj_em", "adj_o", "adj_d", "adj_tempo") ) dark = Theme( color="#e8e8e8", background_color="#14161a", border_color="#2c3038", striped_color="#1b1e23", highlight_color="#262a31", header_style={"color": "#a8adb7", "text-transform": "uppercase", "font-size": "0.8rem"}, page_button_style={"color": "#e8e8e8"}, ) Reactable( top25, columns=[ Column(id="rank", name="#", width=50), reactable_sdv_logos(league="mbb", id="logo", name="", variant="dark", id_system="espn", height=28, width=60), Column(id="team_location", name="Team", min_width=150), Column(id="adj_em", name="Adj. margin"), Column(id="adj_o", name="Adj. offense", style=heat(top25, "adj_o", alpha=0.45)), Column(id="adj_d", name="Adj. defense", style=heat(top25, "adj_d", reverse=True, alpha=0.45)), Column(id="adj_tempo", name="Tempo"), ], theme=dark, striped=True, default_page_size=25, compact=True, )

reactablefmtr is the R package that dresses up reactable cells: data bars, color tiles and scales, pill buttons, icon sets, merged columns, highlights and bubble grids. sdvplot.reactable ports its cell formatters to reactable-py as ordinary reactable.Column objects, with reactablefmtr's semantics and defaults (the same color ramps, buckets and layouts), and adds the SportsDataverse parts: any formatter that takes a color column also takes a team column and a league, filling each cell in that team's color with text that stays readable, and data bars and merged columns can carry the row's logo, headshot or wordmark. Icons are inline SVG and tooltips are the cell's title, so the tables need no Font Awesome and no extra JavaScript. Each formatter takes the frame you pass to Reactable (it reads ranges, buckets and team colors from it) and the column's id. Every section below is one formatter on real data from sportsdataverse-py, across the NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB and college sports. The reactable cookbook covers the logo, headshot and team-color columns these build on. import polars as pl import sportsdataverse.cfb as cfb import sportsdataverse.mbb as mbb import sportsdataverse.mlb as mlb import sportsdataverse.nba as nba import sportsdataverse.nfl as nfl import sportsdataverse.nhl as nhl import sportsdataverse.wnba as wnba from reactable import Column, Reactable, embed_css import sdvplot from sdvplot.reactable import ( reactable_sdv_bubble_grid, reactable_sdv_color_scales, reactable_sdv_color_tiles, reactable_sdv_data_bars, reactable_sdv_highlight, reactable_sdv_icon_assign, reactable_sdv_icon_sets, reactable_sdv_icon_trend, reactable_sdv_logos, reactable_sdv_merge_column, reactable_sdv_pill_buttons, ) NFL_SEASON = 2025 # nflverse and cfbfastR name a season by the year it starts SEASON = 2026 # the 2026 MLB and WNBA seasons, and the 2025-26 NBA, NHL and college basketball seasons embed_css()

reactable_sdv_data_bars draws each value as a bar, its length the value's share of the column's largest. With team_col and league every bar takes its team's primary color, the number inside switches to white on a dark bar, and mark="logo" puts the team's logo at the end of the bar. tooltip=True gives each cell a hover title. The data is the 2025-26 NBA regular season, summed from ESPN team box scores of the regular-season schedule's games (the NBA Cup final, played in December, is not one). # regular-season games only: season_type 2 also holds the NBA Cup final, which does not count in the standings nba_schedule = nba.load_nba_schedule(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( (pl.col("season_type") == 2) & (pl.col("type_abbreviation") == "STD") ) nba_season = ( nba.load_nba_team_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]) .filter(pl.col("game_id").is_in(nba_schedule["game_id"].implode())) .group_by("team_abbreviation", "team_display_name", maintain_order=True) .agg(gp=pl.len(), wins=pl.col("team_winner").sum()) ) assert nba_season["gp"].max() <= 82, "more games than an 82-game regular season" nba_teams = ( nba_season.filter(pl.col("gp") > 10) .sort(["wins", "team_abbreviation"], descending=[True, False]) .head(12) .drop("gp") ) Reactable( nba_teams, columns=[ Column(id="team_abbreviation", show=False), Column(id="team_display_name", name="Team", min_width=190), reactable_sdv_data_bars( nba_teams, team_col="team_abbreviation", league="nba", mark="logo", mark_height=22, bar_height=24, round_edges=True, tooltip=True, id="wins", name="Wins", min_width=320, ), ], default_page_size=12, )
documents.s: 1. Data bars in team colors: NBA wins

documents.t: reactable_sdv_color_tiles fills each cell with a rounded tile on a color ramp: reactablefmtr's default blue-white-orange, or any hex colors you give, here red to green. number_fmt takes a format spec (or a function); the defensive column reverses the ramp because less allowed is better. The team column is tiled too, in each team's own color. Expected points added per play come from nflverse's weekly team stats. weeks = nfl.load_nfl_team_stats([NFL_SEASON]).filter(pl.col("season_type") == "REG") plays = pl.col("attempts") + pl.col("sacks_suffered") + pl.col("carries") def epa_per_play(by): return weeks.group_by(team=by, maintain_order=True).agg( epa=(pl.col("passing_epa") + pl.col("rushing_epa")).sum() / plays.sum() ) nfl_epa = ( epa_per_play(pl.col("team")) .join(epa_per_play(pl.col("opponent_team")), on="team", suffix="_allowed") .with_columns(net=pl.col("epa") - pl.col("epa_allowed")) .sort("net", descending=True) .head(16) ) red_green = ["#d7301f", "#ffffbf", "#1a9850"] Reactable( nfl_epa, columns=[ reactable_sdv_color_tiles(nfl_epa, team_col="team", league="nfl", id="team", name="Team", width=80), reactable_sdv_color_tiles(nfl_epa, colors=red_green, number_fmt="+.3f", id="epa", name="Offense"), reactable_sdv_color_tiles( nfl_epa, colors=red_green[::-1], number_fmt="+.3f", id="epa_allowed", name="Defense allowed" ), reactable_sdv_color_tiles(nfl_epa, colors=red_green, number_fmt="+.3f", bold_text=True, id="net", name="Net"), ], default_page_size=16, compact=True, )
documents.s: 2. Color tiles: NFL offense and defense by EPA

documents.t: reactable_sdv_color_scales is the same scale without the tile: it styles the whole cell, so the table keeps its grid. Run differential is colored on reactablefmtr's default ramp (blue at the bottom, orange at the top), and the team column carries each club's primary color at 85% opacity, its text still readable. The standings are ESPN's for the 2026 season. mlb_table = ( mlb.espn_mlb_standings(season=SEASON) .with_columns(pl.col("wins", "losses", "point_differential").cast(pl.Int64)) .sort(["win_percent", "team_abbreviation"], descending=[True, False]) .select(team="team_abbreviation", name="team_display_name", w="wins", l="losses", diff="point_differential") .head(15) ) Reactable( mlb_table, columns=[ reactable_sdv_color_scales(mlb_table, team_col="team", league="mlb", opacity=0.85, id="team", name=""), Column(id="name", name="Team", min_width=180), Column(id="w", name="W"), Column(id="l", name="L"), reactable_sdv_color_scales(mlb_table, number_fmt="+d", id="diff", name="Run diff."), ], default_page_size=15, compact=True, )

reactable_sdv_pill_buttons sets each value in a rounded pill. Numbers ramp across colors; text takes the first color, or, with team_col, the row's team color. Here the team abbreviation sits in a team-colored pill and points per game ramp from gray to orange. Per-game averages come from ESPN player box scores of the 2026 regular season. schedule = wnba.load_wnba_schedule(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( (pl.col("season_type") == 2) & (pl.col("type_abbreviation") == "STD") ) wnba_players = wnba.load_wnba_player_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).filter( pl.col("game_id").is_in(schedule["game_id"].implode()) & ~pl.col("did_not_play") ) scorers = ( wnba_players.sort("game_date") .group_by("athlete_id", "athlete_display_name", maintain_order=True) .agg(team=pl.col("team_abbreviation").last(), gp=pl.len(), ppg=pl.col("points").mean().round(1)) .filter(pl.col("gp") >= 20) .sort(["ppg", "athlete_display_name"], descending=[True, False]) .head(12) ) Reactable( scorers, columns=[ Column(id="athlete_id", show=False), Column(id="athlete_display_name", name="Player", min_width=180), reactable_sdv_pill_buttons(scorers, team_col="team", league="wnba", bold_text=True, id="team", name="Team"), Column(id="gp", name="GP"), reactable_sdv_pill_buttons(scorers, colors=["#d9d9d9", "#fa4d00"], number_fmt=".1f", id="ppg", name="PPG"), ], default_page_size=12, )
documents.s: 4. Pill buttons: the WNBA's leading scorers

documents.t: reactable_sdv_icon_sets cuts the column into as many quantile buckets as icons (and as colors) and puts the bucket's icon beside each value. Three buckets of goal differential in the final 2025-26 NHL standings get a down arrow, a dash and an up arrow. The icons are inline SVG: circle, square, diamond, triangles, arrows, chevrons, star, check, x, flag, minus, plus, heart and person. nhl_table = ( nhl.nhl_standings("2026-04-16") .select( team="team_abbrev_default", name="team_name_default", pts="points", gf="goal_for", ga="goal_against", diff="goal_differential", ) .sort(["pts", "team"], descending=[True, False]) ) Reactable( nhl_table, columns=[ reactable_sdv_logos(league="nhl", id="team", name="", height=24, width=60), Column(id="name", name="Team", min_width=170), Column(id="pts", name="PTS"), Column(id="gf", name="GF"), Column(id="ga", name="GA"), reactable_sdv_icon_sets( nhl_table, icons=("arrow-down", "minus", "arrow-up"), colors=("#c0392b", "#9e9e9e", "#1e8449"), number_fmt="+d", id="diff", name="Goal diff.", ), ], default_page_size=10, compact=True, )

reactable_sdv_icon_assign repeats an icon up to the column's largest value and fills as many as the row's value: here each SEC team's 2025 wins as filled circles out of the most any team won, with the number to the right. With buckets= it instead fills the row's quantile bucket out of that many icons. Each row reads to a screen reader as an image labelled, for example, "10 out of 13". Wins are counted from cfbfastR's schedule of completed games. games = cfb.load_cfb_schedule(NFL_SEASON).filter(pl.col("completed")) results = pl.concat( [ games.select(team_id="home_id", team="home_team", conference="home_conference", won="home_winner"), games.select(team_id="away_id", team="away_team", conference="away_conference", won="away_winner"), ], how="vertical_relaxed", ) sec = ( results.filter(pl.col("conference") == "SEC") .group_by("team_id", "team") .agg(wins=pl.col("won").sum(), games=pl.len()) .sort(["wins", "team"], descending=[True, False]) .with_columns(logo=pl.col("team_id")) .select("logo", "team", "wins", "games") ) Reactable( sec, columns=[ reactable_sdv_logos(league="cfb", id="logo", name="", id_system="espn", height=24, width=60), Column(id="team", name="Team", min_width=140), reactable_sdv_icon_assign( sec, icon_size=11, fill_color="#461d7c", show_values="right", id="wins", name="Wins", min_width=260 ), Column(id="games", name="Games"), ], default_page_size=16, compact=True, )
documents.s: 6. Icon assign: SEC wins, one dot a win

documents.t: reactable_sdv_icon_trend marks each change with an up icon, a down icon or a dash, and colors the number to match (reactablefmtr's icon_trend_indicator). icons picks the shape: arrow, chevron or triangle. Regular-season wins come from nflverse's schedules of both seasons. nfl_games = nfl.load_nfl_schedule([NFL_SEASON - 1, NFL_SEASON]).filter( (pl.col("game_type") == "REG") & pl.col("result").is_not_null() ) team_wins = ( pl.concat( [ nfl_games.select("season", team="home_team", win=pl.col("result") > 0), nfl_games.select("season", team="away_team", win=pl.col("result") < 0), ] ) .group_by("team", "season") .agg(wins=pl.col("win").sum()) .pivot("season", index="team", values="wins") .rename({str(NFL_SEASON - 1): "before", str(NFL_SEASON): "after"}) .with_columns(change=pl.col("after") - pl.col("before")) .sort(["change", "team"], descending=[True, False]) ) Reactable( team_wins, columns=[ reactable_sdv_logos(league="nfl", id="team", name="", include_name=True, height=24, min_width=100), Column(id="before", name=str(NFL_SEASON - 1)), Column(id="after", name=str(NFL_SEASON)), reactable_sdv_icon_trend( team_wins, icons="triangle", number_fmt="+d", show_zero_label=True, id="change", name="Change" ), ], default_page_size=12, compact=True, )
documents.s: 7. Icon trend: NFL win changes, 2024 to 2025

documents.t: reactable_sdv_merge_column shows a second column's value beside or below each value, so each player's team sits under her name in small gray text. With mark="headshot" (and mark_col naming the ESPN athlete id) the player's photo leads the cell. The merged and id columns are hidden. scorers_named = scorers.join(sdvplot.teams("wnba").select(team="abbr", team_name="name"), on="team", how="left") Reactable( scorers_named, columns=[ reactable_sdv_merge_column( scorers_named, merged_name="team_name", merged_position="below", mark="headshot", mark_col="athlete_id", league="wnba", mark_height=40, id="athlete_display_name", name="Player", min_width=260, ), Column(id="athlete_id", show=False), Column(id="team", show=False), Column(id="team_name", show=False), Column(id="gp", name="GP"), Column(id="ppg", name="PPG"), ], default_page_size=12, )
documents.s: 8. Merge column with headshots: the WNBA scorers again

documents.t: reactable_sdv_highlight bolds a column's maximum (green), minimum (red) or both, optionally on a highlighter. Among the top 20 men's college basketball teams of 2025-26 by adjusted efficiency margin it marks the best and worst adjusted offense; for defense, where lower is better, a (min, max) pair swaps the colors. names = mbb.load_mbb_team_boxscore(seasons=[SEASON]).select("team_id", "team_location").unique("team_id") mbb_ratings = mbb.load_mbb_ratings(SEASON).with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Int32)) # ids ship as text here assert names.schema["team_id"] == mbb_ratings.schema["team_id"] top20 = ( mbb_ratings.sort("rank") .head(20) .join(names, on="team_id", how="left") .with_columns(pl.col("adj_em", "adj_o", "adj_d").round(1), logo=pl.col("team_id")) .select("rank", "logo", "team_location", "adj_em", "adj_o", "adj_d") ) Reactable( top20, columns=[ Column(id="rank", name="#", width=50), reactable_sdv_logos(league="mbb", id="logo", name="", id_system="espn", height=24, width=60), Column(id="team_location", name="Team", min_width=150), Column(id="adj_em", name="Adj. margin"), reactable_sdv_highlight( top20, which="min_max", highlighter=("#fde0dd", "#e5f5e0"), id="adj_o", name="Adj. offense" ), reactable_sdv_highlight( top20, which="min_max", font_color=("green", "red"), highlighter=("#e5f5e0", "#fde0dd"), id="adj_d", name="Adj. defense", ), ], default_page_size=20, compact=True, )
documents.s: 9. Highlights: men's college basketball's best and worst units

documents.t: reactable_sdv_bubble_grid draws each value as a circle (or a square, shape="squares") whose width is its share of the column's largest, up to 100 pixels, colored on a ramp or, with team_col, in the team's color. The Atlantic Division's goals for (primary colors) and against (secondary colors, as squares) make a grid to scan for the big and small numbers. atlantic = ( nhl.nhl_standings("2026-04-16") .filter(pl.col("division_name") == "Atlantic") .sort("division_sequence") .select(team="team_abbrev_default", gf="goal_for", ga="goal_against") ) Reactable( atlantic, columns=[ reactable_sdv_logos(league="nhl", id="team", name="", include_name=True, height=24, min_width=100), reactable_sdv_bubble_grid(atlantic, team_col="team", league="nhl", id="gf", name="Goals for", min_width=120), reactable_sdv_bubble_grid( atlantic, team_col="team", league="nhl", which="secondary", shape="squares", id="ga", name="Goals against", min_width=120, ), ], )
