headshot_url( player_id: Any, league: str, *, id_system: Literal['espn', 'gsis', 'league', 'fox', 'yahoo', 'cbs', 'kenpom', 'ncaa', 'nba_stats', 'wnba_stats'] = 'espn', ) -> str | None A headshot URL for one player.

Name Type Description player_id Any One player id: an ESPN athlete id, an nflverse gsis id, or the league's own player id. league str The SDV league key. "espn" ids work for nfl, nba, wnba, mlb, nhl, cfb, mbb, wbb, nbagl and soccer; "gsis" is NFL only; "league" works for nfl, nba, wnba, mlb, nhl and the 20 HockeyTech leagues (pwhl, ahl, echl, ohl, whl, qmjhl, ushl, sphl, chl, bchl, ajhl, sjhl, ojhl, cchl, gojhl, mhl, nojhl, vijhl, kijhl, mjhl). ESPN files G League (nbagl) photos with the NBA's, so a G League player's ESPN id is the one ESPN uses for him in the NBA. ESPN has photos for only part of the G League and soccer rosters. F1 drivers have none: formula1.com keys its photos by its own driver reference (MAXVER01), not a driver number or Jolpica driver_id. id_system Literal['espn', 'gsis', 'league', 'fox', 'yahoo', 'cbs', 'kenpom', 'ncaa', 'nba_stats', 'wnba_stats'] "espn" (ESPN athlete id, any ESPN league), "gsis" (mapped to ESPN through nflverse's player table, preferring nflverse's own headshot), another provider's player id mapped to its ESPN athlete through sdv-reference-data's {league}_player_aliases ("fox", "yahoo" and "cbs" for nfl and cfb, "ncaa" for cfb, mbb and wbb, "fox" and "yahoo" for nba, wnba, mbb and wbb, "kenpom" for mbb, "nba_stats" for nba, "wnba_stats" for wnba), or "league" (the league's own player id, sdvplotR's id_type = "league": an NBA or WNBA Stats PERSON_ID as nba_api / hoopR / wehoop return it, an MLBAM id, an NHL API id, or the player_id of a HockeyTech feed (the 20 HockeyTech leagues above) on assets.leaguestat.com, on the league's CDN; for the NFL it is the gsis id, the same as "gsis"). An unknown NBA, WNBA, MLB or NHL id gets the CDN's silhouette image; an unknown ESPN or HockeyTech id is a 404, which the adapters treat as any missing image.
str | None: The image URL, or None when the id is missing, malformed, or not in the player table.

InputError: (a ValueError) If league has no ESPN headshots or id_system is not valid for league ("league" names the leagues that have league-id headshots). OfflineError: If id_system is "gsis" (or "league" on "nfl"), or a provider, and the nflverse player table, or the league's player_aliases table, cannot be downloaded and no cached copy exists (a DownloadError, also an OSError, when GitHub answers with an error status). UnsafeDownloadError: (an OSError) If id_system is "gsis" and the player table download is refused: larger than the byte cap, past the deadline, or redirected away from https.

hexbin( x: collections.abc.Sequence[Any], y: collections.abc.Sequence[Any], *, radius: float, ids: collections.abc.Sequence[Any] | None = None, weights: collections.abc.Sequence[Any] | None = None, origin: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0), ) -> list[sdvplot._bins.Bin] Bin points into pointy-top hexagons of circumradius radius, in the points' own units. The port of sdvplot-js hexbin (itself d3-hexbin 0.2.2's): the same lattice, centres and bin order. Each point goes to the centre d3-hexbin picks, which is close to but not exactly the nearest: it compares two candidates in lattice units, so about 1-2% of points sit just outside the hexagon drawn for their bin (22 of 2000 real Brooklyn shots at radius 10). That is faithful to d3-hexbin and sdvplot-js; squares contain every point they bin.

Name Type Description x collections.abc.Sequence[Any] The points' x values (a list, numpy array, or pandas / polars Series). y collections.abc.Sequence[Any] The points' y values, one per x. radius float The hexagon's circumradius, in the points' units (a finite number > 0). ids collections.abc.Sequence[Any] | None Optional link ids, one per point (e.g. a shot id column); each becomes a string, as sdvplot-js's toId (None, NaN and "" become ""). Default: the row number. weights collections.abc.Sequence[Any] | None Optional non-negative weights, one per point, read by position as ids (e.g. points per shot); each bin's weight is the sum of its points'. A missing or non-finite weight counts 0 but the point stays in its bin. Default: every point weighs 1, so weight equals count. origin tuple[float, float] The point a cell centre falls on, (x, y) in the points' units (default (0.0, 0.0)): a hoop-centred lattice, origin = the basket's coordinates. The points are binned relative to it and it is added back to each centre, so ids stay the absolute centre "x,y".

list[Bin] — The non-empty cells in first-seen order, each with id ("x,y", the centre as JavaScript prints it), x, y (-0 folded to 0), rows (the points' 0-based positions), ids, count and weight. A point with a missing (None), NaN or infinite coordinate is in no bin.

InputError: If radius is not a finite number greater than 0, or origin is not two finite numbers. ValueError: If x, y, ids and weights differ in length, a coordinate is not a number, or a weight is negative or not a number.

import sdvplot # three Brooklyn shots of 2025-26 in tenths of a foot from the hoop (sportsdataverse-data # nba_stats_shots): the two at the rim share a 1 ft hexagon bins = sdvplot.hexbin([0, -1, -44], [0, 7, 252], radius=10) [(b.id, b.count) for b in bins] # [('0,0', 2), ('-43.301270189221924,255', 1)]

The HoloViews adapter: a Bokeh plot hook that draws the marks through the Bokeh adapter when the element renders. Name What it is add_bins Hexagonal or square bins, colored by count or weight, on a HoloViews element: the Bokeh adapter's add_bins. add_headshots Draw each player's headshot centred on its (x, y) point of a HoloViews element (Bokeh backend). add_logos Draw each team's logo centred on its (x, y) point of a HoloViews element (Bokeh backend). add_wordmarks Draw each team's wordmark centred on its (x, y) point of a HoloViews element (Bokeh backend). axis_logos Not supported on HoloViews (it draws through Bokeh, which has no axis logos yet).

add_bins( target: Any, x: Any, y: Any, *, shape: Literal['hex', 'square'] = 'hex', radius: float | None = None, side: float | None = None, equal_area: bool = False, ids: Any = None, weights: Any = None, origin: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0), value: Literal['count', 'weight'] = 'count', fill: float | None = None, min_count: int = 1, palette: Any = 'Viridis256', alpha: float = 1.0, link: Any = None, ) -> Any Hexagonal or square bins, colored by count or weight, on a HoloViews element: the Bokeh adapter's add_bins. A Bokeh plot hook draws the cells with sdvplot.bokeh.add_bins when the element renders (one patches glyph named "sdvplot_bins", with its ColumnDataSource of bin_id, count, weight, point_ids and rows), so the cells, ids and colors are the Bokeh adapter's. Only the Bokeh backend is supported. Linking: as Bokeh's, in the browser with no server. Pass the points element of the plot (e.g. the hv.Points in target, or target itself) as link: its rendered ColumnDataSource is linked both ways, so selecting cells (add tools=["tap", "box_select"]) selects their points and selecting points selects their cells. Its rows must be the points of x and y, in that order.

Name Type Description target Any A HoloViews element or overlay. x Any The points' x values, in data units. y Any The points' y values. shape Literal['hex', 'square'] "hex" (the default) or "square". radius float | None The hexagon's circumradius, in data units; for squares, with equal_area=True. side float | None The square's side (shape="square"). equal_area bool Squares of a radius-radius hexagon's area. ids Any Optional link ids, one per point (default the row number); see sdvplot.hexbin. weights Any Optional non-negative weights, one per point (see sdvplot.hexbin): each bin's weight. origin tuple[float, float] The point a cell centre falls on (default (0.0, 0.0)): a hoop-centred lattice, origin = the basket's coordinates. value Literal['count', 'weight'] What the fill encodes: "count" (the default, the points in each cell) or "weight" (the sum of their weights). fill float | None The drawn cell's size as a fraction of the lattice cell, in (0, 1]: default 0.88 for squares (a gap, so they do not touch edge to edge) and 1.0 for hexagons (the tiled hexbin look). min_count int Cells with fewer points are not drawn (default 1, every cell). min_count=2 suits shot charts: single attempts are not drawn. sdvplot.hexbin / squarebin still return every cell. palette Any A Bokeh palette name or list of colors (default "Viridis256"), lowest to highest value. alpha float The cells' fill opacity, 0 to 1. link Any Optional points element of target (or target itself) to link selections with.
element — A clone of target with the hook added.

InputError: If the lattice options are not valid (see sdvplot.binner), value is not "count" or "weight", fill is not in (0, 1], min_count is not a whole number >= 1, or alpha is outside [0, 1]. UnsupportedTargetError: If target is not a HoloViews element or overlay. TypeError: If the current HoloViews backend is not Bokeh. ValueError: If x, y, ids and weights differ in length, or link is not an element of target.

The matplotlib adapter: logos, wordmarks and headshots on Axes, single-Axes Figures and seaborn grids. Name What it is add_bins Draw hexagonal or square bins, colored by count or weight, as one PolyCollection (ax.hexbin). add_headshots Draw each player's headshot centred on its (x, y) point of a matplotlib or seaborn plot. add_images Draw any image, by local path or URL, centred on each (x, y) point of a matplotlib or seaborn plot. add_logos Draw each team's logo centred on its (x, y) point of a matplotlib or seaborn plot. add_wordmarks Draw each team's wordmark centred on its (x, y) point of a matplotlib or seaborn plot. axis_logos Replace a team axis' tick labels with the teams' logos (or wordmarks), or a player axis' with headshots. team_tiers A tier list: each team's logo in its tier's row, tier 1 on top, on a dark (sdvplotR) or light theme. title_image Set the plot title and draw an image (a team logo, or any image) beside it.

add_bins( target: Any, x: Any, y: Any, *, shape: Literal['hex', 'square'] = 'hex', radius: float | None = None, side: float | None = None, equal_area: bool = False, ids: Any = None, weights: Any = None, origin: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0), value: Literal['count', 'weight'] = 'count', fill: float | None = None, min_count: int = 1, **kwargs: Any, ) -> Any Draw hexagonal or square bins, colored by count or weight, as one PolyCollection (ax.hexbin). The cells are sdvplot.binner's, in data units, so a hex chart and a square chart of the same shots (and an sdvplot-js chart of them) bin every point alike. Only cells with points are drawn (ax.hexbin's mincnt=1). The collection's array is the counts (or the weights, value="weight"), so fig.colorbar(ax.collections[-1]) keys it; its gid is "sdvplot_bins" and it keeps the bins as sdvplot_bins (a list of Bin, in draw order). Linking: matplotlib draws static images, so there is no selection to share. With picker=True a pick_event's event.ind indexes sdvplot_bins, whose rows and ids name the points in the cell.

Axes — The Axes drawn on.

perspective_sdv_config( frame: Any, *, team_col: str, league: str, plugin: str = 'Datagrid', theme: str | None = None, mode: Literal['light', 'dark'] = 'light', logo_col: str | None = None, background: str | None = None, formats: dict[str, dict[str, Any] | None] | None = None, season: Any = None, id_system: Literal['auto', 'team_id', 'espn', 'espn_abbr', 'nhl', 'nflverse', 'mlbstats', 'nba_api', 'hockeytech', 'ncaa', 'pff', 'cricinfo', 'cfbd', 'bref', 'sportsipy', 'fangraphs', 'yahoo', 'kenpom', 'torvik', 'sdvplotr', 'name', 'nhl_id', 'fox', 'cbs', 'sports247', 'on3'] = 'auto', strict: bool = False, ) -> dict[str, Any] A Perspective viewer config that colors each team by its own colors, for the Datagrid or a chart. The colors are the shared team palette (as the deck.gl and pydeck adapters use), taken over the teams in sorted order: each team's color, made 3:1 against the background and ΔE 20 from every earlier team's, so a team keeps one color whatever the frame's order. Perspective takes a palette, not a color per value, so each palette lists those colors in the order Perspective hands colors out (checked in Chromium on Perspective 5.5.1): plugin="Datagrid": the team column's cells are filled (bg_mode "series"; Perspective picks a readable text color). The grid gives the palette to the values in the order it first draws them, so it is in the frame's order of first appearance: keep the grid's rows in the frame's order (no sort), and keep it to about one row per team. In a long grid, scrolling past a team the grid has not drawn yet shifts every later color. Null cells take no color and no palette slot. Only a text team column (string, or a pandas category / polars Categorical or Enum, which Perspective loads as strings) is filled: Perspective rejects a fill on a number column, so a numeric team id column gets none, with one warning. a chart plugin: the view is yours. Split a bar, line or area chart by the team (split_by=[team_col]) and each team's series takes its color from every numeric column's palette, in sorted order, because Perspective sorts split values. Put the team column in an "X/Y Scatter"'s Color slot (its third column) and each team's points take theirs from the team column's palette, in the frame's order, the order Perspective meets them (a scatter's split_by draws one panel per team instead). Perspective sorts split values by codepoint (upper case first: "LSU" before "Louisiana"), as Python does. Null team values split into a "null" series that comes first and takes the first palette entry, so the sorted palette then starts with the fallback grey. Checked on "X Bar", "Y Bar", "Y Line" and "X/Y Scatter"; a Treemap or Sunburst hands colors out in drawing order, which this does not follow. Every numeric column also gets a number format (number_format, Intl.NumberFormat options): 3 decimals for a float (rates, EPA), 1 for a float whose name says it is a percentage (pct, percent), and an integer plain (no grouping: 2024, not 2,024). formats overrides them.

Name Type Description frame Any The data the viewer shows: a polars or pandas DataFrame (anything narwhals reads eagerly). team_col str The column holding team identifiers (any id system resolve reads). league str The SDV league key, e.g. "nfl". plugin str The Perspective plugin: "Datagrid" (the default) or a chart's name. theme str | None A registry table theme (sdv_table_themes()). On the Datagrid it sets the font family and size (plugin_config), each numeric column's sign colors (its neg and pos) and, when the theme has a numeric face of its own, the numeric columns' font. Perspective quotes the value as one family name (no fallback stack), so the page must load the font itself (Google Fonts), or the browser draws its default font. Charts take no fonts from a config. mode Literal['light', 'dark'] "light" or "dark": the Perspective theme ("Pro Light" or "Pro Dark") and the registry theme's mode. logo_col str | None A logo URL column (perspective_logo_column) to show as links on the Datagrid. Perspective 5.5's Datagrid draws no images, so a link is the one format a URL column has. formats dict[str, dict[str, Any] | None] | None Per column, a number_format (Intl.NumberFormat options, e.g. {"maximumFractionDigits": 2}) to use instead of the default, or None for none. background str | None The color the teams must read against. import polars as pl from sdvplot.perspective import perspective_sdv_config # 2024 regular season, offense: EPA per play (nflverse play-by-play) epa = pl.DataFrame({"posteam": ["BAL", "BUF", "DET"], "epa_per_play": [0.218, 0.1885, 0.1592]}) cfg = perspective_sdv_config(epa, team_col="posteam", league="nfl", theme="datagolf") print(cfg["columns_config"]["posteam"]["bg_color"]) bars = perspective_sdv_config(epa, team_col="posteam", league="nfl", plugin="Y Bar") bars |= {"group_by": ["posteam"], "split_by": ["posteam"], "columns": ["epa_per_play"]} # in a notebook: PerspectiveWidget(epa, **cfg)

pitch_coords( data: Any, *, provider: str, x: str | None = None, y: str | None = None, flip: bool | str | None = None, pitch_length: float | None = None, pitch_width: float | None = None, ) -> Any Convert soccer event coordinates from any provider's frame to the pitch surface("soccer") draws. Opta and Wyscout run 0-100 on both axes and are not to scale, StatsBomb uses 120 x 80, tracking providers use meters or centimeters from the center spot, and ESPN reports the distance from the attacked goal as a fraction of half the pitch. This converts any of them to one frame: meters, origin at the center spot, a regulation 105 x 68 m pitch, attacking toward +x, with +y on the attacker's left. The conversion is piecewise-linear between pitch landmarks (goal line, six-yard line, penalty spot, box edge and halfway line along the pitch; touchline, box side, six-yard side and post across it), so a shot on the edge of an Opta box lands on the edge of the regulation box; points beyond the outermost landmark are extrapolated, not clamped. The landmarks come from mplsoccer and ship in sdvplot/data/pitch_landmarks.csv, byte-identical to sdvplotR's. ESPN's frame is derived from Opta's (opta_x = 100 - 50 * x, opta_y = 100 * (1 - y)), and ESPN's (0, 0) "no location" becomes null. Event providers record every action as if the team attacked left to right; flip turns rows half a turn (pitch_x and pitch_y both change sign) so two teams attack opposite ends with each wing on its own side.

Name Type Description data Any A pandas or polars DataFrame of events. provider str The frame of data: "opta" (alias "statsperform"), "wyscout", "statsbomb", "uefa", "impect", "espn", "tracab" (cm), "skillcorner", "secondspectrum" (m) or "metrica" (0-1). Case is ignored. x str | None The x column; None uses the provider's usual name ("field_position_x" for ESPN, as sportsdataverse-py's espn_soccer_game_plays returns it; "x" otherwise). y str | None The y column; None uses "field_position_y" for ESPN, "y" otherwise. flip bool | str | None None (no row flipped), True/False for every row, or the name of a boolean column with no missing values. pitch_length float | None The venue's length in meters (90-120), for tracking providers only. pitch_width float | None The venue's width in meters (45-90), for tracking providers only.

DataFrame — data's type, with pitch_x (meters along the pitch: -52.5 is the defended goal line, 52.5 the attacked one) and pitch_y (meters across: -34 to 34, positive = the attacker's left) added as Float64; existing columns of those names are replaced in place, every other column is kept. Nulls stay null.

TypeError: If data is not a pandas/polars DataFrame, provider is not a string, x/y is not a string, flip has the wrong type, or a coordinate column is boolean or another non-numeric type. InputError: If provider is unknown, pitch_length/pitch_width are given to a fixed-frame provider, missing for a tracking one or out of range, x and y name the same column, a column is missing, a string is not a number, or the flip column is not boolean or has missing values.

import polars as pl import sdvplot shots = pl.DataFrame({"x": [88.5, 83, 50], "y": [50.0, 21.1, 100.0], "away": [False, True, False]}) out = sdvplot.pitch_coords(shots, provider="opta", flip="away") out["pitch_x"].to_list() # [41.5, -36.0, 0.0]: the spot, the far box edge, halfway ax = sdvplot.surface("soccer") ax.scatter(out["pitch_x"], out["pitch_y"], zorder=20)

The Plotly adapter: logos, wordmarks, headshots and axis logos as layout images on a Plotly Figure. Name What it is add_bins Draw hexagonal or square bins, colored by count or weight, on a Plotly Figure. add_headshots Draw each player's headshot centred on its (x, y) point of a Plotly figure. add_logos Draw each team's logo centred on its (x, y) point of a Plotly figure, as layout images. add_wordmarks Draw each team's wordmark centred on its (x, y) point of a Plotly figure. axis_logos Replace a category axis' team labels with the teams' logos (or wordmarks), or a player axis' with headshots. link_script The JavaScript that links add_bins' cells to a points trace in a static HTML file, with no Python running.

add_bins( target: Any, x: Any, y: Any, *, shape: Literal['hex', 'square'] = 'hex', radius: float | None = None, side: float | None = None, equal_area: bool = False, ids: Any = None, weights: Any = None, origin: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0), value: Literal['count', 'weight'] = 'count', fill: float | None = None, min_count: int = 1, colorscale: Any = 'Viridis', opacity: float = 1.0, xref: str = 'x', yref: str = 'y', ) -> Any Draw hexagonal or square bins, colored by count or weight, on a Plotly Figure. The cells are sdvplot.binner's, in data units: one path layout shape per cell (layer="below", so traces draw over it), filled from colorscale by value (count or weight). One scatter trace named "sdvplot_bins" holds a marker at each centre (invisible until selected) that carries the cell for interaction: ids are the bin ids ("x,y", as sdvplot-js stamps data-sdv-id), customdata each cell's point ids, the marker colors the values (and draw the colorbar), and hovering a cell shows its count and weight. Linking: in a static HTML file, pass sdvplot.plotly.link_script(fig) to fig.write_html(post_script=...) (or to_html): plotly.js handlers then link cell and point selections and hover in the browser, with no Python. In a FigureWidget (or Dash) the link is a callback instead: selecting cells gives points.point_inds; the customdata of those markers are the point ids (the row numbers when no ids were given), which set a points trace's selectedpoints. The other way, set the bins trace's selectedpoints to the cells whose customdata holds a selected point. sdvplot.bin_ids gives a table the same key.

Name Type Description target Any A plotly.graph_objects.Figure (or FigureWidget). x Any The points' x values, in the axes' data units. y Any The points' y values. shape Literal['hex', 'square'] "hex" (the default) or "square". radius float | None The hexagon's circumradius, in data units; for squares, with equal_area=True. side float | None The square's side (shape="square"). equal_area bool Squares of a radius-radius hexagon's area. ids Any Optional link ids, one per point (default the row number); see sdvplot.hexbin. weights Any Optional non-negative weights, one per point (see sdvplot.hexbin): each bin's weight. origin tuple[float, float] The point a cell centre falls on (default (0.0, 0.0)): a hoop-centred lattice, origin = the basket's coordinates. value Literal['count', 'weight'] What the fill encodes: "count" (the default, the points in each cell) or "weight" (the sum of their weights). fill float | None The drawn cell's size as a fraction of the lattice cell, in (0, 1]: default 0.88 for squares (a gap, so they do not touch edge to edge) and 1.0 for hexagons (the tiled hexbin look). min_count int Cells with fewer points are not drawn (default 1, every cell). min_count=2 suits shot charts: single attempts are not drawn. sdvplot.hexbin / squarebin still return every cell. colorscale Any A Plotly colorscale name or list (default "Viridis"), mapped from the fewest to the most points. opacity float The cells' opacity, 0 to 1. xref str The x axis to draw on ("x", "x2", ...), for subplots: the shapes' xref and the trace's xaxis. yref str The y axis to draw on ("y", "y2", ...).
Figure — target, with the shapes and the trace added.

InputError: If the lattice options are not valid (see sdvplot.binner), value is not "count" or "weight", fill is not in (0, 1], min_count is not a whole number >= 1, or opacity is outside [0, 1]. UnsupportedTargetError: If target is not a Plotly Figure. ValueError: If x, y and ids differ in length, or xref/yref does not name an x/y axis.

link_script( target: Any, *, points: int = 0, bins: int | None = None, ) -> str The JavaScript that links add_bins' cells to a points trace in a static HTML file, with no Python running. Pass it to fig.write_html(post_script=...) or fig.to_html(post_script=...): Plotly runs it after the plot is drawn (its {plot_id} placeholder becomes the div's id). It registers plotly.js handlers on the div: selecting cells (box or lasso select) selects their points on the points trace, selecting points selects the cells holding them, double-click deselects both, and hovering a cell highlights its points until the pointer leaves. A point belongs to a cell when its link id is among the cell's customdata: the points trace's own customdata (its first element when each is a list) as a string, as sdvplot.hexbin writes ids, else its row number, which is add_bins' default id. The figure is read once, now: call it after the traces are final.

Name Type Description target Any A plotly.graph_objects.Figure that add_bins drew on. points int The index of the points trace in fig.data (default 0, the first trace). bins int | None The index of the bins trace (default the last trace named "sdvplot_bins").

UnsupportedTargetError: If target is not a Plotly Figure. ValueError: If the figure has no add_bins trace, bins is not one, or points is not the index of another trace.

Name Type Description data Any A pandas or polars DataFrame with tier_no (1 is the top tier) and team (any id system resolve() understands), and optionally tier_rank, the position within the tier; without it, teams keep their order in data. league str The SDV league key, e.g. "nfl". title str | None The title; None gives "{LEAGUE} Team Tiers", "" none. subtitle str | None The subtitle; None or "" for none. caption str | None The caption; None for none. tier_desc dict[Any, str] | None Each tier's label, keyed by tier number; None gives sdvplotR's (1 "Elite" ... 5 "What are they doing?"). Labels wrap at 15 characters; a tier without one gets none. presort bool Sort teams alphabetically within each tier (ignores tier_rank). alpha float Logo opacity, 0 to 1. height float | None Logo height as a fraction of the panel height; None gives 0.1, about the largest height at which 32 logos in 5 tiers (7, 7, 6, 6, 6) neither overlap nor leave the panel at the default 6.4 x 4.8 in figure. no_line_below_tier Any A tier number, or several, with no separator line below. devel bool Draw each team as text instead of its logo (fast, and needs no download). theme Literal['dark', 'light'] "dark" (sdvplotR's: a near-black background) or "light" (white). variant str The logo variant: "auto" (the default) draws the archive's "dark" variant, a mark made for dark backgrounds, on the dark theme and "default" on the light one; a team with no dark mark draws its default one, with no warning. With a surface_layer among them, the deck has a top-down OrthographicView (y up) fitted to the surface, and every other layer is drawn in the surface's own coordinates. logo_icon_layer( rows: 'Any', *, x: 'str', y: 'str', team: 'str', league: 'str', season: 'Any' = None, variant: 'str' = 'default', id_system: 'IdSystem' = 'auto', strict: 'bool' = False, size: 'float' = 32, alpha: 'float' = 1.0, id: 'str' = 'sdvplot-logos', ) -> 'dict[str, Any]' pydeck IconLayer props drawing each row's team logo at its (x, y). The logos are deck.gl's auto-packed icons: deck.gl fetches each URL once and packs it into its own atlas, 128 px tall at the logo's aspect, centred on the point. A team with no logo (or one that does not resolve) is left out with one warning, as the other adapters do; so is a row with a missing x or y. x and y are in the layer's coordinates: longitude and latitude on a map, or a surface's own units over surface_layer (deck sets the coordinate system for you).

Name Type Description rows 'Any' The rows: a polars or pandas DataFrame, or a sequence of mappings. x 'str' The column of each logo's x (a longitude on a map, or a surface's x). y 'str' The column of each logo's y. team 'str' The column of each row's team (abbreviation, name or id; see id_system). league 'str' The SDV league key, e.g. "nhl". season 'Any' A season for every row, or the name of a column holding each row's season. variant 'str' The logo variant, e.g. "dark". id_system 'IdSystem' How the team values are read. strict 'bool' Raise UnresolvedTeamError for a team that does not resolve, instead of warning. size 'float' The logo's height on screen in px, 1 or more (deck.gl's getSize in "pixels" units). alpha 'float' The layer's opacity in [0, 1]. id 'str' The layer id.

InputError: (a ValueError) If a column is not in rows, size is under 1 px, alpha is outside [0, 1], or league, season, variant or id_system is not valid. UnresolvedTeamError: With strict=True, for a team that does not resolve. OfflineError: If the logo manifest is neither cached nor downloadable.

import sdvplot.pydeck # Arrowhead and Lincoln Financial Field, by longitude and latitude stadiums = [ {"team": "KC", "lon": -94.4839, "lat": 39.0489}, {"team": "PHI", "lon": -75.1675, "lat": 39.9008}, ] props = sdvplot.pydeck.logo_icon_layer(stadiums, x="lon", y="lat", team="team", league="nfl", size=40) assert [d["team"] for d in props["data"]] == ["12", "21"]

pass_arc_layer( rows: 'Any', *, x: 'str', y: 'str', xend: 'str', yend: 'str', team: 'str', league: 'str', season: 'Any' = None, id_system: 'IdSystem' = 'auto', strict: 'bool' = False, which: 'Which' = 'primary', background: 'str | None' = None, fallback: 'str' = '#808080', width: 'float' = 2, alpha: 'float' = 1.0, height: 'float | None' = None, tilt: 'float | None' = None, id: 'str' = 'sdvplot-arcs', ) -> 'dict[str, Any]' pydeck ArcLayer props: one arc per row from (x, y) to (xend, yend), in the team's colors. The team's primary color is at the source and its secondary at the target (which="secondary" swaps them), so where the two colors differ the ends tell the direction. Each team keeps one color per end, the teams taken in the order they first appear. With background, every color keeps 3:1 contrast against it (dark mode) and stays distinct (CIE76 ΔE of 20 or more) from the other teams' colors at that end. Caveat: a color that does not read gives way to the team's other color, so when only one of a team's two colors reads on the background, both ends take it and the arcs no longer show their direction (France's navy and mint on a dark pitch are both mint); pick a background on which both read (France's both read on a mid-tone green such as #4a7f3a), or check that sourceColor and targetColor differ. A team that does not resolve takes fallback as given, outside the palette; a row with a missing coordinate is left out with one warning.

Name Type Description rows 'Any' The rows: a polars or pandas DataFrame, or a sequence of mappings. x 'str' The column of each arc's source x. y 'str' The column of each arc's source y. xend 'str' The column of each arc's target x. yend 'str' The column of each arc's target y. team 'str' The column of the team each arc is colored by. league 'str' The SDV league key, e.g. "soccer". season 'Any' The season the teams are resolved for. id_system 'IdSystem' How the team values are read. strict 'bool' Raise UnresolvedTeamError for a team that does not resolve, instead of warning (and drawing it in fallback). which 'Which' The color at the source end, "primary" or "secondary"; the target end takes the other. background 'str | None' The background the arcs are drawn on; given, each color keeps 3:1 contrast against it and stays distinct from the other teams'. fallback 'str' The color of a team that does not resolve, or has no color (an unresolved team's is used as given). width 'float' The arc's width in px, 1 or more. alpha 'float' The layer's opacity in [0, 1]. height 'float | None' deck.gl's getHeight, how high each arc rises for its length, 0 or more (0 draws a straight line). None (the default) keeps deck.gl's 1; lower, such as 0.3, keeps arcs laid flat (tilt=90) close to their chord, inside the surface. tilt 'float | None' deck.gl's getTilt, degrees in [-90, 90]: 90 lays each arc flat on the surface, so a top-down 2D view shows the curve. None (the default) keeps deck.gl's upright arcs, for a pitched 3D view. id 'str' The layer id.

dict — pydeck.Layer keyword arguments: type "ArcLayer", data (one dict per arc: source, target, sourceColor and targetColor as [r, g, b, a], team (the resolved id, else the row's value as text) and the row's index), the accessors get_source_position, get_target_position, get_source_color and get_target_color, get_width, width_units, opacity and, with height and tilt, get_height and get_tilt.

InputError: (a ValueError) If a column is not in rows, width is under 1 px, alpha is outside [0, 1], height is negative, tilt is outside [-90, 90], which is not "primary" or "secondary", or league, season or id_system is not valid. UnresolvedTeamError: With strict=True, for a team that does not resolve. ValueError: If background or fallback is not a hex color.

import sdvplot.pydeck # two of France's passes in the 2018 World Cup final (StatsBomb open data through SPADL, metres) passes = [ {"team": "478", "start_x": 54.69, "start_y": 6.38, "end_x": 56.44, "end_y": 1.28}, {"team": "478", "start_x": 22.31, "start_y": 9.78, "end_x": 6.56, "end_y": 31.88}, ] props = sdvplot.pydeck.pass_arc_layer( passes, x="start_x", y="start_y", xend="end_x", yend="end_y", team="team", league="soccer", id_system="team_id", tilt=90, ) assert props["data"][0]["sourceColor"] == [0, 0, 128, 255] # France's navy at the passer assert props["data"][0]["targetColor"] != props["data"][0]["sourceColor"] # its mint at the receiver

surface_layer( sport: str, league: str, *, id: str = 'sdvplot-surface', tolerance: float | None = None, **sportypy_kwargs: Any, ) -> dict[str, Any] pydeck PolygonLayer props drawing sportypy's playing surface for sport and league. The surface is in its own coordinates: deck.gl's "cartesian" coordinate system, in the surface's units (feet for a rink, metres for a pitch) with the origin at its centre, the frame sportypy draws in and NHL api-web's shot coordinates are in. Each closed loop of a visible sportypy feature is one data row (a faceoff circle is two: its half rings, a goaltender trapezoid two: its strips; a loop that crosses itself, which only odd updates make, is split at the crossing into loops that do not, and a loop with no area is left out), in sportypy's drawing order (its zorder), filled with its color (alpha included); a hidden one (a #rrggbb00 fill, or none) is left out. sportypy draws arcs with up to 8,000 points (80,000 before sportypy 1.2.2); each loop is thinned to tolerance (see below), which leaves an NHL rink about 14,400 points instead of 123,000, and the coordinates are rounded to 0.0001 of the unit, so a deck stays a few hundred kilobytes. sdvplot-js's surfaceLayer draws sporty's own geometry, so the two languages' vertices differ (the props, colors and extents agree).

Name Type Description sport str The sportypy sport: "hockey", "soccer", "basketball", "football", "baseball", "softball", "lacrosse", "tennis", "volleyball" or "curling". league str sportypy's league code for the sport, e.g. "nhl", "fifa", "nba". id str The layer id. tolerance float | None The simplification distance, in the surface's units; None for a 2,000th of the surface's diagonal (about 0.11 ft on an NHL rink), 0 to keep every point. Each loop caps it at its own mean width and keeps both ends of every segment at least that long, so thin lines and rings keep their corners and shape (every loop within 5% of its area unthinned, measured on all ten sports). **sportypy_kwargs Any Passed to the sportypy surface class: rink_updates / pitch_updates / court_updates / field_updates, color_updates, units.

dict — pydeck.Layer keyword arguments: type "PolygonLayer", data (one dict per closed loop of a feature: name, sportypy's class name in snake case, polygon and fillColor as [r, g, b, a]), the accessors get_polygon and get_fill_color, coordinate_system "'cartesian'" (quoted, a constant), filled and stroked.
InputError: (a ValueError) If sportypy has no surface for sport, no league for it, or tolerance is negative. OptionalDependencyError: If sportypy 1.2 or newer (the surfaces extra) is not installed.

import sdvplot.pydeck rink = sdvplot.pydeck.surface_layer("hockey", "nhl") assert rink["coordinate_system"] == "'cartesian'" # quoted: a constant, not an expression assert rink["data"][0]["name"] == "defensive_zone"

The pygal adapter: logos, wordmarks and headshots on pygal XY charts, plus team colors as a pygal Style. Name What it is add_bins Hexagonal or square bins, colored by count or weight, as SVG polygons on a pygal XY chart. add_headshots Draw each player's headshot centred on its (x, y) point of a pygal XY chart, in every render of the chart. add_logos Draw each team's logo centred on its (x, y) point of a pygal XY chart, in every render of the chart. add_wordmarks Draw each team's wordmark centred on its (x, y) point of a pygal XY chart, in every render of the chart. axis_logos Not supported: pygal draws axis labels as text nodes, so sdvplot.pygal cannot put logos in their place. team_style A pygal Style whose series colors are the teams' colors, in the order the series are added.

add_bins( chart: Any, x: Any, y: Any, *, shape: Literal['hex', 'square'] = 'hex', radius: float | None = None, side: float | None = None, equal_area: bool = False, weights: Any = None, origin: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0), value: Literal['count', 'weight'] = 'count', fill: float | None = None, min_count: int = 1, low: str = '#deebf7', high: str = '#08519c', opacity: float = 1.0, ) -> Any Hexagonal or square bins, colored by count or weight, as SVG polygons on a pygal XY chart. As the marks: add_bins records the cells on the chart and one xml filter (chart.add_xml_filter) draws them at each render, through chart.view, pygal's own projection, so each vertex sits where pygal would draw that point. The cells go under pygal's series, clipped to the plot area; each is a <polygon> with a <title> (its bin_id, count and weight, the browser's hover text). The fill runs from low (the lowest value) to high (the highest), in RGB. Linking: none, pygal's SVG is static.

Name Type Description chart Any A pygal XY-family chart (pygal.XY, DateTimeLine, ...). x Any The points' x values, in the chart's x units. y Any The points' y values. shape Literal['hex', 'square'] "hex" (the default) or "square". radius float | None The hexagon's circumradius, in data units; for squares, with equal_area=True. side float | None The square's side (shape="square"). equal_area bool Squares of a radius-radius hexagon's area. weights Any Optional non-negative weights, one per point (see sdvplot.hexbin): each bin's weight. origin tuple[float, float] The point a cell centre falls on (default (0.0, 0.0)): a hoop-centred lattice, origin = the basket's coordinates. value Literal['count', 'weight'] What the fill encodes: "count" (the default, the points in each cell) or "weight" (the sum of their weights). fill float | None The drawn cell's size as a fraction of the lattice cell, in (0, 1]: default 0.88 for squares (a gap, so they do not touch edge to edge) and 1.0 for hexagons (the tiled hexbin look). min_count int Cells with fewer points are not drawn (default 1, every cell). min_count=2 suits shot charts: single attempts are not drawn. sdvplot.hexbin / squarebin still return every cell. low str The color of the lowest value (default "#deebf7"), any CSS color. high str The color of the highest value (default "#08519c"). opacity float The cells' fill opacity, 0 to 1.
chart — chart, with the cells recorded.

InputError: If the lattice options are not valid (see sdvplot.binner), value is not "count" or "weight", fill is not in (0, 1], min_count is not a whole number >= 1, or opacity is outside [0, 1]. UnsupportedTargetError: If chart is not an XY-family chart. ValueError: If x, y and weights differ in length, or low / high is not a color.

import pygal from sdvplot.pygal import add_bins # three Brooklyn shots of 2025-26, legacy tenths of a foot (sportsdataverse-data nba_stats_shots) x, y = [0, -1, -44], [0, 7, 252] chart = pygal.XY(stroke=False) chart.add("shots", list(zip(x, y))) add_bins(chart, x, y, shape="square", side=15, opacity=0.7) svg = chart.render()

add_headshots( chart: Any, x: Any, y: Any, players: Any, *, league: str, height: float = 0.1, alpha: float = 1, embed: bool = False, id_system: str = 'espn', ) -> Any Draw each player's headshot centred on its (x, y) point of a pygal XY chart, in every render of the chart. Copy the chart with copy.deepcopy (the copy keeps the headshots); a shallow copy shares pygal's own series and filters.

Name Type Description chart Any A pygal XY chart or one of its time variants (DateTimeLine, DateLine, ...). x Any The points' x positions in the chart's units (read by position). y Any The points' y positions, the same length as x. players Any The player id for each point. league str The SDV league key, e.g. "nfl". height float The headshot height as a fraction of the plot height, in (0, 1]. alpha float Opacity, 0 to 1. embed bool True puts the image bytes in the SVG as data URIs (no network when rendering). id_system str "espn" (ESPN athlete ids), "gsis" (NFL) or "league" (the league's own player id: nfl gsis, NBA and WNBA Stats ids, MLBAM, NHL), as in headshot_url.
object — chart itself, with a filter that draws the headshots whenever it renders.

InputError: (a ValueError) If height or alpha is out of range, league has no ESPN headshots, or id_system is not valid for league. ValueError: If the inputs differ in length. UnsupportedTargetError: (a TypeError) If chart is not an XY-family chart. OfflineError: If the nflverse player table (id_system="gsis"), or with embed=True a headshot, is neither cached nor downloadable (a DownloadError, also an OSError, for an HTTP error status). UnsafeDownloadError: (an OSError) If a download is refused: larger than the byte cap, past the deadline, or redirected away from https.
import pygal import sdvplot chart = pygal.XY(stroke=False) chart.add("passing", [(4.2, 0.31)]) sdvplot.add_headshots(chart, [4.2], [0.31], ["3139477"], league="nfl", height=0.15)
sdvplotR geom_nfl_headshots()

add_logos( chart: Any, x: Any, y: Any, teams: Any, *, league: str, season: Any = None, height: float = 0.1, alpha: float = 1, variant: str = 'default', embed: bool = False, id_system: str = 'auto', ) -> Any Draw each team's logo centred on its (x, y) point of a pygal XY chart, in every render of the chart. Copy the chart with copy.deepcopy (the copy keeps the logos); a shallow copy shares pygal's own series and filters.

Name Type Description chart Any A pygal XY chart (XY(stroke=False) for a scatter) or a DateTimeLine/DateLine/ TimeLine/TimeDeltaLine. x Any The points' x positions in the chart's units (numbers, or dates for the time charts; read by position). y Any The points' y positions, the same length as x. teams Any The team for each point, in any id system resolve() understands. league str The SDV league key, e.g. "nfl". season Any One season, or one per point, to pick each team's mark for that era. height float The logo height as a fraction of the plot height, in (0, 1]. alpha float Opacity, 0 to 1. variant str "default", "dark", or a named variant from marks(). embed bool True puts the image bytes in the SVG as data URIs, so the SVG and render_to_png() need no network. id_system str The id system of teams; "auto" tries each in order.
object — chart itself, with a filter that draws the logos whenever it renders.

InputError: (a ValueError) If height or alpha is out of range, league, id_system or variant is unknown, or season is not a year or is outside the seasons sdvplot knows for the league. ValueError: If x/y/teams differ in length. UnsupportedTargetError: (a TypeError) If chart is not an XY-family chart (Bar, Line and Pie place values by category or angle). OfflineError: If the logo manifest, or with embed=True a mark's image, is neither cached nor downloadable (a DownloadError, also an OSError, when the CDN answers with an error status; an IntegrityError when it sends a file that does not match the manifest's sha256). UnsafeDownloadError: (an OSError) If a download is refused: larger than the byte cap, past the deadline, or redirected away from https. UnsafeCachePathError: (a ValueError) If embed=True and the manifest's sha256 or extension for a mark would put the file outside the cache directory.

import pygal import sdvplot chart = pygal.XY(stroke=False) chart.add("games", [(10, -3), (20, -7)]) sdvplot.add_logos(chart, [10, 20], [-3, -7], ["KC", "BUF"], league="nfl", height=0.15) chart.render_to_file("chart.svg")

reactable-py columns (pip install sdvplot[reactable]), ported from sdvplotR's reactable_sdv_* functions, plus reactablefmtr's cell formatters (data bars, color tiles and scales, pills, icons, merged columns, highlights, bubbles). Name What it is reactable_sdv_args The Reactable keyword arguments that make a table look like a registry or reactablefmtr theme. reactable_sdv_bubble_grid A reactable column of circles (or squares) sized and colored by value, by a color column, or by team. reactable_sdv_color_scales A reactable column whose cell backgrounds are filled on a color scale, by a color column, or in team colors. reactable_sdv_color_tiles A reactable column of rounded tiles filled on a color scale, by a color column, or in the row's team color. reactable_sdv_cols_label One reactable column per team-named column of data (a KC column, a BUF column, ...), its header reactable_sdv_data_bars A reactable column of horizontal bars sized by value, in a scale color, a color column or the team color. reactable_sdv_frame A Reactable with a title and subtitle above it and a legend and source line under it, in a Google font. reactable_sdv_gauge A reactable column that draws each cell's number as a half-circle gauge (an inline SVG) with the value inside. reactable_sdv_headshots A reactable column that shows each cell's player id as the player's headshot. reactable_sdv_highlight A reactable column whose highest (or lowest, or both) values are bold, in a color, optionally on a highlight. reactable_sdv_icon_assign A reactable column that repeats an icon, filled up to the value: a rating in stars, a count in dots. reactable_sdv_icon_legend An icon legend: each icon, in its color, before its label, for reactable_sdv_frame(legend=...). reactable_sdv_icon_sets A reactable column that puts an icon beside each number, chosen by the value's quantile bucket. reactable_sdv_icon_trend A reactable column that marks each change with an up arrow, a down arrow or a dash, the value colored to match. reactable_sdv_legend A color legend: a row of swatches with a label under each, for reactable_sdv_frame(legend=...). reactable_sdv_logos A reactable column that shows each cell's team as its logo. reactable_sdv_merge_column A reactable column that shows a second column's value beside or below each value, after an optional mark. reactable_sdv_pill_buttons A reactable column whose values sit in rounded pills, in a scale color, a color column or the team color. reactable_sdv_sparkbar A reactable column that draws each cell's list of numbers as a small bar chart (an inline SVG). reactable_sdv_sparkline A reactable column that draws each cell's list of numbers as a sparkline (an inline SVG). reactable_sdv_team_color_bar A reactable column whose cells hold a bar in the row's team color, as long as the value's share of the maximum. reactable_sdv_team_color_bg A reactable column whose cells are filled with the row's team color, mostly transparent. reactable_sdv_theme One of reactablefmtr's 27 table themes, or any of the 122 surveyed registry themes (sdv_table_themes()). reactable_sdv_theme_team A table theme in a team's colors: the header filled with the primary color squarebin( x: collections.abc.Sequence[Any], y: collections.abc.Sequence[Any], *, side: float, ids: collections.abc.Sequence[Any] | None = None, weights: collections.abc.Sequence[Any] | None = None, origin: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0), ) -> list[sdvplot._bins.Bin] Bin points into axis-aligned squares of side side, in the points' own units. The port of sdvplot-js squarebin. As in d3-hexbin's lattice a cell is centred on the origin, so centres are (i * side, j * side). Cells are half-open, [c - side/2, c + side/2) on each axis: a point exactly on an edge goes to the higher cell, because the cell index is JavaScript's Math.round(x / side) (halves round up, also below zero: -5 with side 10 is in the cell at 0). With origin the centres are origin + (i * side, j * side).

Name Type Description x collections.abc.Sequence[Any] The points' x values (a list, numpy array, or pandas / polars Series). y collections.abc.Sequence[Any] The points' y values, one per x. side float The square's side, in the points' units (a finite number > 0). ids collections.abc.Sequence[Any] | None Optional link ids, one per point; as in hexbin. Default: the row number. weights collections.abc.Sequence[Any] | None Optional non-negative weights, one per point; as in hexbin. Default: weight equals count. origin tuple[float, float] The point a cell centre falls on (default (0.0, 0.0)): a hoop-centred lattice, origin = the basket's coordinates; as in hexbin.
list[Bin] — The non-empty cells in first-seen order, as hexbin returns them.

InputError: If side is not a finite number greater than 0, or origin is not two finite numbers. ValueError: If x, y, ids and weights differ in length, a coordinate is not a number, or a weight is negative or not a number.

Name Type Description league str | None An SDV league key such as "nfl"; None returns every league. include_conferences bool Also list the conference and league rows (sdvplotR's include_conferences): the college conferences of cfb, mbb and wbb, the AFC, NFC and NFL, MLB with the AL and NL, the NBA and WNBA with their East and West, the NHL with its division marks, the AAF, and the NCAA in every college league. Their program is "conference" or "league", their team_id and abbr the short name ("SEC", "Big 12", "AFC", "East"), their colors cbbplotR's (color_source "cbbplotR") or the placeholder, and a team's conference_id equals its conference row's. The default, False, lists teams only, so code that loops over teams sees only teams; conferences are opt-in everywhere (resolve and palette never answer one). The mark helpers (logo_url, marks, add_logos and the rest) do draw one, by this key, from the archive's conference, league and division marks ("SEC", "Big 12", "AFC", "NFL", "MLB").

polars.DataFrame — The index columns league, team_id, abbr, name, short_name, location, program, conference_id, conference, color_primary, color_secondary and color_source: "nflverse", "espn" or "openf1" (published colors), "logo" (derived from the team's archived logo, where no source publishes any), "cbbplotR" (a conference row's) or "fallback" (a placeholder). In soccer, one pool of ESPN club ids, conference_id and conference are a club's domestic league (ESPN's slug and name: "eng.1", "English Premier League"), null for a national team (program "national").
InputError: (a ValueError) If league is given and is not a known league key.
import polars as pl import sdvplot sdvplot.teams("nfl").shape # (32, 12) sdvplot.teams("cfb", include_conferences=True).filter(pl.col("program") == "conference")["abbr"]
sdvplotR sdv-py

Shared behaviour every adapter must have. Adapter test suites call check_adapter_contract(). Name What it is check_adapter_contract Raise an AssertionError naming the broken rule if the adapter breaks the sdvplot adapter contract. check_table_adapter_contract Raise an AssertionError naming the broken rule (T0-T6) if a table adapter breaks the table contract.

check_adapter_contract( adapter: module, make_target: collections.abc.Callable[[], Any], *, league: str = 'nfl', known: tuple[str, str] = ('LV', 'LAR'), known_wordmarks: tuple[str, str] = ('LV', 'LAC'), players: tuple[str, str] = ('3139477', '4241479'), make_axis_target: collections.abc.Callable[[list[str]], Any] | None = None, ) -> None Raise an AssertionError naming the broken rule if the adapter breaks the sdvplot adapter contract. The rules, and the test hooks the adapter must expose, are in this module's docstring.

Name Type Description adapter module The adapter module under test (it exposes add_logos, add_wordmarks, add_headshots, axis_logos and the _drawn_marks hook). make_target collections.abc.Callable[[], Any] Builds a fresh target (a plot) to draw on each time it is called. league str The SDV league key the checks run in. known tuple[str, str] Two team ids of league that have logos. known_wordmarks tuple[str, str] Two team ids of league that have wordmarks. players tuple[str, str] Two player ids of league that have headshots. make_axis_target collections.abc.Callable[[list[str]], Any] | None make_axis_target(categories) builds a target whose x axis shows those categories, in order. Required when the adapter supports axis logos (rule 7).
None — Returns normally when every rule holds.

AssertionError: Naming the broken rule ("rule N: ..."), when the adapter breaks it. UnsupportedTargetError: (a TypeError) If no adapter is registered for the library of make_target()'s object (register the adapter before checking it). InputError: (a ValueError) If league is unknown. OfflineError: If the logo manifest, which the checks read for the expected marks, is neither cached nor downloadable (a DownloadError, also an OSError, when the CDN answers with an error status). A download error inside an adapter call is reported as the AssertionError of the rule that made the call. UnsafeDownloadError: (an OSError) If the manifest download is refused: larger than the byte cap, past the deadline, or redirected away from https.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from sdvplot import matplotlib as adapter from sdvplot.testing import check_adapter_contract def make_target(): _, ax = plt.subplots() ax.set_xlim(0, 30) ax.set_ylim(-10, 0) return ax def make_axis_target(categories): _, ax = plt.subplots() ax.bar(categories, range(1, len(categories) + 1)) return ax check_adapter_contract(adapter, make_target=make_target, make_axis_target=make_axis_target)

palette and team_colors give you colors keyed by team, so a chart can be colored without hand-picking hex codes. import sdvplot import polars as pl df = pl.DataFrame({"team": ["KC", "BUF", "PHI", "DET"], "epa": [0.12, 0.10, 0.09, 0.15]}) df team epa KC 0.12 BUF 0.1 PHI 0.09 DET 0.15

palette accepts a polars Series of abbreviations, so it can be passed straight to seaborn. import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import seaborn as sns sns.barplot( df.to_pandas(), x="team", y="epa", hue="team", palette=sdvplot.palette("nfl", teams=df["team"]), legend=False, ) plt.show()

team_colors returns one color per team, in the order given. which="secondary" picks the secondary color. sdvplot.team_colors("nfl", df["team"], which="secondary") shape: (4,) Series: 'team' [str] [ "#ffb612" "#c60c30" "#a5acaf" "#b0b7bc" ]

The palette is a plain dict of team -> hex, so other libraries take it directly (not executed here). Plotly: import plotly.express as px px.bar(df.to_pandas(), x="team", y="epa", color="team", color_discrete_map=sdvplot.palette("nfl", teams=df["team"])) Altair: import altair as alt p = sdvplot.palette("nfl", teams=df["team"]) alt.Chart(df.to_pandas()).mark_bar().encode( x="team", y="epa", color=alt.Color("team", scale=alt.Scale(domain=list(p), range=list(p.values()))), )

color_source says where each team's colors come from: nflverse or espn when a source publishes them, logo when they are the two dominant colors of the team's current logo (an approximation, for a team no source publishes colors for), and fallback for a placeholder from a colorblind-safe palette that only keeps teams apart. Check color_source before treating a color as a team's own. No source publishes OHL colors, so the colors below are read from each team's logo; every NFL team has colors from nflverse. sdvplot.teams("ohl").select("team_id", "name", "color_primary", "color_source").head() team_id name color_primary color_source 1 Brantford Bulldogs #ba8748 logo 10 Kitchener Rangers #233e95 logo 11 Owen Sound Attack #eec943 logo 12 Sudbury Wolves #a63039 logo 13 Flint Firebirds #0d1d41 logo

headshot_url builds a player headshot url from an id. ESPN athlete ids work directly; other id systems are translated through a table (for NFL, nflverse's gsis ids). import sdvplot

An ESPN athlete id works as is; an NFL gsis id goes through the nflverse player table. sdvplot.headshot_url(3139477, "nfl") 'https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/headshots/nfl/players/full/3139477.png' sdvplot.headshot_url("00-0033873", "nfl", id_system="gsis") 'https://static.www.nfl.com/image/upload/t_headshot_desktop/f_auto/league/wdckwtob1lybvkmxnf7p.png'

The url is an ordinary image link. Here the gsis one is downloaded and shown. import io import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import requests from PIL import Image url = sdvplot.headshot_url("00-0033873", "nfl", id_system="gsis") img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(requests.get(url, timeout=30).content)) plt.imshow(img) plt.axis("off") plt.show()
Other leagues use their ESPN athlete id the same way, for example a men's college basketball player: sdvplot.headshot_url(4433134, "mbb")

Nine charts and tables from the 2025 college football season: all 136 FBS teams on one scatter, conference small multiples, a conference standings table, the national champion's season, a rivalry, FCS upsets, an interactive Altair chart, a ranked bar chart and a tier list. The data comes from the cfbfastR releases and ESPN through sportsdataverse.cfb. import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import polars as pl import sportsdataverse.cfb as cfb import sdvplot SEASON = 2025 CAPTION = f"Data: cfbfastR via sportsdataverse-py | {SEASON} season" # sdvplot team ids are strings: cast the loaders' integer ESPN ids once, here summaries = cfb.load_cfb_team_summaries([SEASON]).select( pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Utf8), "pos_team", "conference", "EPAplay_off", "EPAplay_def" ) schedule = cfb.load_cfb_schedule([SEASON]).with_columns(pl.col("home_id", "away_id").cast(pl.Utf8)) names = sdvplot.teams("cfb").select("team_id", school="short_name") summaries.height, schedule.height (136, 3831)

Offensive EPA per play against defensive EPA per play allowed, from the cfbfastR team summaries. With this many teams the logos have to be small: height=0.045 makes each one 4.5% of the plot's height. fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6)) ax.axvline(summaries["EPAplay_off"].mean(), color="grey", lw=0.8, ls="--") ax.axhline(summaries["EPAplay_def"].mean(), color="grey", lw=0.8, ls="--") ax.scatter(summaries["EPAplay_off"], summaries["EPAplay_def"], s=0) ax.margins(0.06) sdvplot.add_logos( ax, summaries["EPAplay_off"], summaries["EPAplay_def"], summaries["team_id"], league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=0.045, ) ax.invert_yaxis() ax.set(xlabel="Offense EPA per play", ylabel="Defense EPA per play allowed (better is up)") ax.set_title(f"Every FBS offense and defense, {SEASON}", loc="left", fontweight="bold") fig.text(0.99, 0.01, CAPTION, ha="right", fontsize=8, color="grey") plt.show()
documents.s: 1. All 136 FBS teams on one chart

documents.t: The same data, one panel per conference: every FBS team as a grey dot behind, the conference's own teams as logos. The grey layer gets a copy of the data without the conference column, so plotnine repeats it in every panel. from plotnine import aes, facet_wrap, geom_point, ggplot, labs, scale_y_reverse, theme, theme_minimal from sdvplot.plotnine import geom_sdv_logos ( ggplot(summaries.to_pandas(), aes("EPAplay_off", "EPAplay_def")) + geom_point(data=summaries.drop("conference").to_pandas(), color="#d9d9d9", size=1) + geom_sdv_logos(aes(team="team_id"), league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=0.13) + facet_wrap("conference", ncol=4) + scale_y_reverse() + labs( x="Offense EPA per play", y="Defense EPA per play allowed", title=f"FBS offense and defense by conference, {SEASON}", caption=CAPTION, ) + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(10, 6)) )

Big Ten records built from the schedule: conference games and all games through the regular season (the title game and bowls left out). gt_sdv_logos turns the id column into logos and gt_fmt_tally writes each pair of win and loss columns as one record. from great_tables import GT from sdvplot.great_tables import gt_fmt_tally, gt_sdv_logos, gt_theme_athletic regular = schedule.filter(pl.col("completed"), pl.col("season_type") == "regular", pl.col("week") <= 14) sides = pl.concat( [ regular.select( "conference_game", team_id="home_id", conf="home_conference", pf="home_points", pa="away_points" ), regular.select( "conference_game", team_id="away_id", conf="away_conference", pf="away_points", pa="home_points" ), ] ).with_columns(win=pl.col("pf") > pl.col("pa")) big_ten = ( sides.filter(pl.col("conf") == "Big Ten") .group_by("team_id", maintain_order=True) .agg( conf_w=(pl.col("win") & pl.col("conference_game")).sum(), conf_l=(~pl.col("win") & pl.col("conference_game")).sum(), w=pl.col("win").sum(), l=(~pl.col("win")).sum(), pf=pl.col("pf").sum(), pa=pl.col("pa").sum(), ) .join(names, on="team_id") .sort(["conf_w", "w", "pf"], descending=True) .select("team_id", "school", "conf_w", "conf_l", "w", "l", "pf", "pa") ) ( GT(big_ten) .pipe(gt_sdv_logos, "team_id", league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=24) .pipe(gt_fmt_tally, ["conf_w", "conf_l"], label="Conf") .pipe(gt_fmt_tally, ["w", "l"], label="Overall") .cols_label(team_id="", school="", pf="PF", pa="PA") .tab_header(title=f"Big Ten standings, {SEASON}", subtitle="Regular season, before the title game") .tab_source_note(CAPTION) .pipe(gt_theme_athletic, density="compact") )

Indiana went 16-0. Each bar is one game's margin in Indiana's primary color, the opponent's logo above it, and title_image puts the Indiana logo beside the title. resolve turns the school name into its id. from sdvplot.matplotlib import title_image team = sdvplot.resolve("Indiana", "cfb") games = ( schedule.filter(pl.col("completed"), (pl.col("home_id") == team) | (pl.col("away_id") == team)) .sort("start_date") .with_columns( home=pl.col("home_id") == team, opponent=pl.when(pl.col("home_id") == team).then("away_id").otherwise("home_id"), ) .with_columns( margin=pl.when(pl.col("home")) .then(pl.col("home_points") - pl.col("away_points")) .otherwise(pl.col("away_points") - pl.col("home_points")) ) ) game_no = list(range(1, games.height + 1)) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5)) ax.bar(game_no, games["margin"], color=sdvplot.team_colors("cfb", team), width=0.7) sdvplot.add_logos(ax, game_no, games["margin"] + 7, games["opponent"], league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=0.08) ax.set_ylim(0, games["margin"].max() + 14) ax.set_xticks(game_no) ax.set(xlabel="Game", ylabel="Margin of victory") ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False) record = f"{(games['margin'] > 0).sum()}-{(games['margin'] < 0).sum()}" title_image( ax, team, f"Indiana's {record} national title season, {SEASON}", league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=30, loc="left", fontweight="bold", ) fig.text( 0.99, 0.01, "Data: ESPN via sportsdataverse-py | opponents' logos above each bar", ha="right", fontsize=8, color="grey", ) plt.show()
documents.s: 4. The national champion's season, with a logo in the title

documents.t: Ohio State against Michigan since 2004 (load_cfb_schedule for 22 seasons). Each bar is the margin from Ohio State's side, colored for the winner, with the winner's logo at the end of the bar. osu, mich = sdvplot.resolve(["Ohio State", "Michigan"], "cfb") history = cfb.load_cfb_schedule(list(range(2004, SEASON + 1))).with_columns(pl.col("home_id", "away_id").cast(pl.Utf8)) rivalry = ( history.filter(pl.col("home_id").is_in([osu, mich]), pl.col("away_id").is_in([osu, mich]), pl.col("completed")) .with_columns( osu_margin=pl.when(pl.col("home_id") == osu) .then(pl.col("home_points") - pl.col("away_points")) .otherwise(pl.col("away_points") - pl.col("home_points")) ) .with_columns(winner=pl.when(pl.col("osu_margin") > 0).then(pl.lit(osu)).otherwise(pl.lit(mich))) .sort("season") ) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5)) ax.bar(rivalry["season"], rivalry["osu_margin"], color=sdvplot.team_colors("cfb", rivalry["winner"]).to_list()) tip = rivalry["osu_margin"] + pl.Series([8 if m > 0 else -8 for m in rivalry["osu_margin"]]) sdvplot.add_logos(ax, rivalry["season"], tip, rivalry["winner"], league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=0.08) ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8) ax.text(2020, 2, "no game", ha="center", fontsize=8, color="grey", rotation=90, va="bottom") ax.set_ylim(-35, 50) ax.set(ylabel="Ohio State margin") ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False) ax.set_title("The Game: Ohio State vs Michigan, 2004-2025", loc="left", fontweight="bold") fig.text(0.99, 0.01, "Data: ESPN via sportsdataverse-py", ha="right", fontsize=8, color="grey") plt.show()

The index has every FBS and FCS program and most of Division II and III. The 2025 schedule also lists opponents outside the NCAA divisions (NAIA schools, mostly); most of those do not resolve, and sdvplot says so in one warning instead of guessing. import warnings opponents = pl.concat( [ schedule.select(team_id="home_id", division="home_division"), schedule.select(team_id="away_id", division="away_division"), ] ).unique("team_id", maintain_order=True) with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: warnings.simplefilter("always") resolved = sdvplot.resolve(opponents["team_id"], "cfb") print(str(caught[0].message)[:160], "...") ( opponents.with_columns(found=resolved.is_not_null()) .group_by("division", maintain_order=True) .agg(teams=pl.len(), in_sdvplot=pl.col("found").sum()) .sort("teams", descending=True) ) 33 value(s) did not resolve to a cfb team: '15' (unknown), '2366' (unknown), '127991' (unknown), '110254' (unknown), '2395' (unknown), '2939' (unknown), '108358 ... division teams in_sdvplot iii 240 237 ii 162 158 fbs 136 136 fcs 129 129 null 32 6 FCS teams have their own logos and colors, so an FCS-over-FBS upset draws like any other game. In 2025 the FCS won four of its games against FBS teams: cross = schedule.filter( pl.col("completed"), pl.concat_list("home_division", "away_division").list.sort() == ["fbs", "fcs"], ) fcs_home = pl.col("home_division") == "fcs" upsets = cross.filter(pl.when(fcs_home).then("home_winner").otherwise("away_winner")).select( winner=pl.when(fcs_home).then("home_id").otherwise("away_id"), loser=pl.when(fcs_home).then("away_id").otherwise("home_id"), score=pl.format( "{}-{}", pl.max_horizontal("home_points", "away_points"), pl.min_horizontal("home_points", "away_points") ), week="week", ) rows = list(range(upsets.height, 0, -1)) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5)) ax.set(xlim=(0, 1), ylim=(0.4, upsets.height + 0.6)) ax.axis("off") sdvplot.add_logos(ax, [0.2] * upsets.height, rows, upsets["winner"], league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=0.17) sdvplot.add_logos(ax, [0.8] * upsets.height, rows, upsets["loser"], league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=0.17) for y, row in zip(rows, upsets.iter_rows(named=True), strict=True): ax.text(0.5, y, f"{row['score']}\nweek {row['week']}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11) ax.text(0.2, upsets.height + 0.55, "FCS winner", ha="center", fontweight="bold") ax.text(0.8, upsets.height + 0.55, "FBS loser", ha="center", fontweight="bold") ax.set_title( f"FCS over FBS: {upsets.height} upsets in {cross.height} games, {SEASON}", loc="left", fontweight="bold", pad=18 ) plt.show()
documents.s: 6. FBS, FCS and the schools sdvplot does not know

documents.t: The cfbfastR opponent-adjusted ratings (load_cfb_ratings) as an Altair chart with tooltips. add_logos layers the logos onto the chart; the transparent points underneath carry the tooltips. import altair as alt ratings = ( cfb.load_cfb_ratings([SEASON]) .with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Utf8)) .join(names, on="team_id") .select("team_id", "school", "adj_off_epa", "adj_def_epa", "adj_net", "net_rank") ) points = ( alt.Chart(ratings.to_pandas()) .mark_circle(size=250, opacity=0) .encode( x=alt.X("adj_off_epa", title="Adjusted offense EPA per play"), y=alt.Y("adj_def_epa", title="Adjusted defense EPA per play (better is up)", scale=alt.Scale(reverse=True)), tooltip=["school", "net_rank", alt.Tooltip("adj_net", format=".3f")], ) .properties(width=640, height=440, title=f"Opponent-adjusted FBS ratings, {SEASON}") ) sdvplot.add_logos( points, ratings["adj_off_epa"], ratings["adj_def_epa"], ratings["team_id"], league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=0.05 )

ESPN's final 2025 FPI (load_cfb_fpi_weekly, the snapshot after the title game), top 25. The bars use the teams' ESPN colors and axis_logos(ax, "y") replaces the team ids on the axis. fpi = cfb.load_cfb_fpi_weekly([SEASON]).filter(pl.col("season_type") == 3) top = ( fpi.select(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Utf8), "fpi") .sort("fpi", descending=True) .head(25) .reverse() # barh draws from the bottom up, so number one ends on top ) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 6)) ax.barh(top["team_id"], top["fpi"], color=sdvplot.team_colors("cfb", top["team_id"]).to_list()) for y, value in enumerate(top["fpi"]): ax.text(value + 0.3, y, f"{value:.1f}", va="center", fontsize=8) sdvplot.axis_logos(ax, "y", league="cfb", season=SEASON, height=0.04) ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False) ax.set_xlabel("FPI (points better than an average FBS team)") ax.set_title(f"Final FPI top 25, {SEASON}", loc="left", fontweight="bold") fig.text(0.99, 0.01, "Data: ESPN FPI via sportsdataverse-py", ha="right", fontsize=8, color="grey") plt.show()
documents.s: 8. A ranked bar chart with logos on the y axis

documents.t: A composite ranking: the average of each team's rank in two systems, cfbfastR's adjusted net EPA and FEI. The top 32 go into five tiers with team_tiers, on its default dark theme: it draws each school's dark-background logo, so Ohio State, Texas A&M and Penn State stay visible. from sdvplot.matplotlib import team_tiers composite = ( cfb.load_cfb_ratings([SEASON]) .with_columns(pl.col("team_id").cast(pl.Utf8), score=(pl.col("net_rank") + pl.col("fei_net_rank")) / 2) .sort("score", "net_rank", "team_id") .head(32) ) sizes = [4, 6, 7, 7, 8] # teams per tier, top to bottom composite = composite.with_columns(tier_no=pl.Series([tier for tier, n in enumerate(sizes, start=1) for _ in range(n)])) fig = team_tiers( composite.select("tier_no", team="team_id"), "cfb", title=f"College football tiers, {SEASON}", subtitle="average rank in adjusted net EPA and FEI", caption=CAPTION, alpha=1, tier_desc={1: "Elite", 2: "Contenders", 3: "Very good", 4: "Good", 5: "Solid"}, ) plt.show()
